**Running means launching the actual app and interacting with it** —
not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a
`console.log`. The app as a user (human or programmatic) would meet
it: the CLI at its command, the server at its socket, the GUI at its
window.

## First: does a project skill already cover this?

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path —
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed
what worked: the exact `apt-get` line, the env vars, the patches, the
driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

```bash
d=$PWD; while :; do
  grep -Hm1 '^description:' "$d"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null
  [ -e "$d/.git" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break
  d=$(dirname "$d")
done
```

- **One describes launching/driving this app** → read that SKILL.md
  and follow it verbatim. Don't paraphrase; don't skip the patches.
- **Mega-repo, several plausible, no clear match** → ask the user
  which unit to run.
- **Stale** (fails on mechanics unrelated to your task) → tell the
  user; offer to refresh it via `/run-skill-generator`.
- **Nothing about running** → fall back to the patterns below.

## Otherwise: match the shape, use the pattern

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section — you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web
app, [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) — drive it with
`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) — it has the `_electron`
REPL driver skeleton and the tmux wrapping.

## Drive it, don't just launch it

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app — it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to
a point where a user would see something:

- CLI → type a representative command, check the exit code and output.
- Server → hit the route the diff touches with `curl`, read the body.
- TUI → `send-keys` a navigation, `capture-pane` the result.
- GUI → click the button, screenshot the window. **Look at the
  screenshot.** A blank frame is a failure to launch.

If the fallback pattern didn't work out of the box — you had to
install packages, set env vars, patch config, or write a driver —
recommend `/run-skill-generator` in your report so that work gets
captured as a project skill. If it just worked, don't.

**Running means launching the actual app and interacting with it** —
not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a
`console.log`. The app as a user (human or programmatic) would meet
it: the CLI at its command, the server at its socket, the GUI at its
window.

## First: does a project skill already cover this?

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path —
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed
what worked: the exact `apt-get` line, the env vars, the patches, the
driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

```bash
d=$PWD; while :; do
  grep -Hm1 '^description:' "$d"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null
  [ -e "$d/.git" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break
  d=$(dirname "$d")
done
```

- **One describes launching/driving this app** → read that SKILL.md
  and follow it verbatim. Don't paraphrase; don't skip the patches.
- **Mega-repo, several plausible, no clear match** → ask the user
  which unit to run.
- **Stale** (fails on mechanics unrelated to your task) → tell the
  user; offer to refresh it via `/run-skill-generator`.
- **Nothing about running** → fall back to the patterns below.

## Otherwise: match the shape, use the pattern

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section — you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web
app, [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) — drive it with
`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) — it has the `_electron`
REPL driver skeleton and the tmux wrapping.

## Drive it, don't just launch it

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app — it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to
a point where a user would see something:

- CLI → type a representative command, check the exit code and output.
- Server → hit the route the diff touches with `curl`, read the body.
- TUI → `send-keys` a navigation, `capture-pane` the result.
- GUI → click the button, screenshot the window. **Look at the
  screenshot.** A blank frame is a failure to launch.

If the fallback pattern didn't work out of the box — you had to
install packages, set env vars, patch config, or write a driver —
recommend `/run-skill-generator` in your report so that work gets
captured as a project skill. If it just worked, don't.

   export function renderPageNavigator(pages, currentPage, newspaper, onSelectPage) {

4. Errors and fixes:

   - **Cleanup query too broad (occurred twice):** First occurrence used `created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '2 hours'` and deleted 27 unrelated newspaper rows (including 2 with `status: 'finalised'`) instead of just the test's own row. Disclosed transparently to the user in the next response. Second occurrence: repeated the same mistake pattern once more before self-correcting mid-session. **Fix applied and now standing practice:** always query the specific test user's `id` and match `newspapers.created_by = <that id>` (or track exact inserted IDs from setup script output) before deleting — verified via a `SELECT` first when in doubt (e.g., checking `created_by` on candidate rows before deleting).

   - **Drawer toggle wiped unsaved inspector data:** The first implementation of `toggleSidebar()`/`closeSidebar()` (later renamed `toggleStoryPicker`/`closeStoryPicker`) called the shared `render()` function, which rebuilds the Inspector from `state` — but `applyStoryToInspector()` populates `<input>` values by direct DOM mutation, bypassing `state` entirely. Closing the drawer after selecting a story therefore silently reverted the populated (but unsaved) headline field to empty, causing a Playwright test timeout (`.newspaper-section.filled` never appeared because the save button's headline was blank). **Fix:** made all drawer-visibility toggles pure `classList.toggle()` DOM operations with no `render()` call, exactly matching how the sidebar behaved before it became a drawer.

   - **Lopsided ~3500px-tall page from CSS Grid stretch:** Removing `.workspace-shell`'s `height`/`overflow:hidden` entirely (to allow "some scrolling") let one long grid-row child (the 20+-item Editions list) stretch the WHOLE row height via Grid's default `align-items: stretch`, dragging the empty canvas/inspector columns down with it. **Fix:** reverted to a fixed-height (`height: calc(100vh - 60px)`), `overflow: hidden` shell, with `overflow-y: auto` scoped individually to `.sidebar-panel`, `.canvas-scroll`, and `.workspace-inspector` — "some scrolling is fine" correctly means per-panel scrolling, not whole-page scrolling.

   - **Static compact canvas width still overflowed on shorter screens:** Tried `max-width: 420px` for Fit mode first; measured via Playwright at 1366×768 that `canvasScrollHeight` (659px) still exceeded `canvasClientHeight` (587px) by ~72px — a fixed guessed width can't account for viewport-height variance. **Fix:** switched to `height: 100%; width: auto; max-width: 100%` (height-relative, CSS-computed from the actual container size) — re-measured, `scrollHeight === clientHeight` exactly, confirmed at any viewport height by construction.

   - **`vw`-relative font sizing broke down under the new layout (predicted, then confirmed):** `.newspaper-section strong` used `clamp(0.7rem, 1.6vw, 1.05rem)` — approximated the canvas's actual size only when canvas width tracked viewport width ~1:1, which stopped being true after the sidebar-drawer change (canvas became a fraction of viewport width) and again after the Fit-mode height-driven sizing. I flagged this as a predicted risk in PROJECT_STATUS.md's Follow-up 5 debt section without confirming it broken. The user's next screenshot (at their real 170%-zoom setup) showed it WAS broken — text overflowing section boxes and overlapping neighbors. **Fix:** switched to CSS container queries — added `container-type: inline-size` to `.canvas-scroll .newspaper-canvas`, changed `.newspaper-section strong`/`small` and `.section-label` from `vw` to `cqw` units, verified via screenshot at a viewport approximating the user's exact zoom scenario (1129×650) that overflow was fully resolved.

   - **`git add` pathspec failure (recurring mechanical issue, twice):** Running `git add <list including an already-git-rm'd path>` fails entirely with "fatal: pathspec '...' did not match any files" and stages NOTHING from that command (not even the valid paths). **Fix applied both times:** re-ran `git add` without the already-deleted path (which was already staged from the earlier `git rm`), producing two separate commits per logical change — accepted and documented as a "continuation" commit rather than treated as an error requiring a fix to git behavior itself.

   - Resolved text legibility at small canvas sizes using CSS container queries instead of viewport units — a durable, zoom-level-and-mode-independent solution rather than another guessed constant.

not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a

it: the CLI at its command, the server at its socket, the GUI at its

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path —
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed
what worked: the exact `apt-get` line, the env vars, the patches, the
driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

```bash
d=$PWD; while :; do
  grep -Hm1 '^description:' "$d"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null
  [ -e "$d/.git" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break
  d=$(dirname "$d")
done
```

- **One describes launching/driving this app** → read that SKILL.md

## Otherwise: match the shape, use the pattern

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section — you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,

**Running means launching the actual app and interacting with it** —
not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a
`console.log`. The app as a user (human or programmatic) would meet
it: the CLI at its command, the server at its socket, the GUI at its
window.

## First: does a project skill already cover this?

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path —
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed
what worked: the exact `apt-get` line, the env vars, the patches, the
driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

```bash
d=$PWD; while :; do
  grep -Hm1 '^description:' "$d"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null
  [ -e "$d/.git" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break
  d=$(dirname "$d")
done
```

- **One describes launching/driving this app** → read that SKILL.md
  and follow it verbatim. Don't paraphrase; don't skip the patches.
- **Mega-repo, several plausible, no clear match** → ask the user
  which unit to run.
- **Stale** (fails on mechanics unrelated to your task) → tell the
  user; offer to refresh it via `/run-skill-generator`.
- **Nothing about running** → fall back to the patterns below.

## Otherwise: match the shape, use the pattern

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section — you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web
app, [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) — drive it with
`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) — it has the `_electron`
REPL driver skeleton and the tmux wrapping.

## Drive it, don't just launch it

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app — it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to
a point where a user would see something:

- CLI → type a representative command, check the exit code and output.
- Server → hit the route the diff touches with `curl`, read the body.
- TUI → `send-keys` a navigation, `capture-pane` the result.
- GUI → click the button, screenshot the window. **Look at the
  screenshot.** A blank frame is a failure to launch.

If the fallback pattern didn't work out of the box — you had to
install packages, set env vars, patch config, or write a driver —
recommend `/run-skill-generator` in your report so that work gets

Large Newspaper Workspace

- typography
- image information
- section properties

- 10–50 editorial sections on one page
- 24+ pages in one edition

   - The specific bug pattern of calling a full `render()` (which rebuilds all DOM from `state`) when only a DOM-only, out-of-`state` mutation (like `applyStoryToInspector`, which directly sets `<input>` values) needs to be preserved — fixed by making UI-only toggles (drawer open/close) pure `classList.toggle()` operations instead.
   - Playwright (`playwright-core`) browser automation for smoke testing, installed fresh each session in a scratchpad directory (`/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/browsertest/`) since it doesn't persist between sessions, pointed at system Chrome (`/usr/bin/google-chrome`).
   - Test-data hygiene discipline: **always clean up test fixtures (temp users, seeded news_items, newspapers) using exact IDs or `created_by` matching — never a time-window (`created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL`) query**, established as a hard rule after two separate incidents where a broad time-window delete removed unrelated rows (disclosed transparently to the user both times).
   - `git add` with a mix of real file paths and one already-deleted (via `git rm`) path fails entirely with "fatal: pathspec ... did not match any files" — requires splitting into two separate commits (the deletion, staged from `git rm`, commits alone first; a follow-up commit picks up the rest).

   export function renderStoryPicker(currentPage, reporterNews, selectedSectionKey, onSelectStory) {

   ```js
   export function renderPageNavigator(pages, currentPage, newspaper, onSelectPage) {
     const container = document.getElementById("pageSwitcher");
     if (!container) return;
     container.innerHTML = pages.map((page) => {
       const active = currentPage && page.id === currentPage.id;
       const filled = (page.sections || []).some((section) => section.headline);
       return `<button class="page-pill${active ? " active" : ""}${filled ? " filled" : ""}" data-page-id="${page.id}" title="Page ${page.page_number}">${page.page_number}</button>`;
     }).join("");
     container.querySelectorAll(".page-pill").forEach((btn) => {
       btn.addEventListener("click", () => onSelectPage(Number(btn.dataset.pageId)));
     });
   }
   ```

4. Errors and fixes:

   - **Cleanup query too broad (occurred twice):** First occurrence used `created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '2 hours'` and deleted 27 unrelated newspaper rows (including 2 with `status: 'finalised'`) instead of just the test's own row. Disclosed transparently to the user in the next response. Second occurrence: repeated the same mistake pattern once more before self-correcting mid-session. **Fix applied and now standing practice:** always query the specific test user's `id` and match `newspapers.created_by = <that id>` (or track exact inserted IDs from setup script output) before deleting — verified via a `SELECT` first when in doubt (e.g., checking `created_by` on candidate rows before deleting).

   - **Drawer toggle wiped unsaved inspector data:** The first implementation of `toggleSidebar()`/`closeSidebar()` (later renamed `toggleStoryPicker`/`closeStoryPicker`) called the shared `render()` function, which rebuilds the Inspector from `state` — but `applyStoryToInspector()` populates `<input>` values by direct DOM mutation, bypassing `state` entirely. Closing the drawer after selecting a story therefore silently reverted the populated (but unsaved) headline field to empty, causing a Playwright test timeout (`.newspaper-section.filled` never appeared because the save button's headline was blank). **Fix:** made all drawer-visibility toggles pure `classList.toggle()` DOM operations with no `render()` call, exactly matching how the sidebar behaved before it became a drawer.

   - **Lopsided ~3500px-tall page from CSS Grid stretch:** Removing `.workspace-shell`'s `height`/`overflow:hidden` entirely (to allow "some scrolling") let one long grid-row child (the 20+-item Editions list) stretch the WHOLE row height via Grid's default `align-items: stretch`, dragging the empty canvas/inspector columns down with it. **Fix:** reverted to a fixed-height (`height: calc(100vh - 60px)`), `overflow: hidden` shell, with `overflow-y: auto` scoped individually to `.sidebar-panel`, `.canvas-scroll`, and `.workspace-inspector` — "some scrolling is fine" correctly means per-panel scrolling, not whole-page scrolling.

   - **Static compact canvas width still overflowed on shorter screens:** Tried `max-width: 420px` for Fit mode first; measured via Playwright at 1366×768 that `canvasScrollHeight` (659px) still exceeded `canvasClientHeight` (587px) by ~72px — a fixed guessed width can't account for viewport-height variance. **Fix:** switched to `height: 100%; width: auto; max-width: 100%` (height-relative, CSS-computed from the actual container size) — re-measured, `scrollHeight === clientHeight` exactly, confirmed at any viewport height by construction.

   - **`vw`-relative font sizing broke down under the new layout (predicted, then confirmed):** `.newspaper-section strong` used `clamp(0.7rem, 1.6vw, 1.05rem)` — approximated the canvas's actual size only when canvas width tracked viewport width ~1:1, which stopped being true after the sidebar-drawer change (canvas became a fraction of viewport width) and again after the Fit-mode height-driven sizing. I flagged this as a predicted risk in PROJECT_STATUS.md's Follow-up 5 debt section without confirming it broken. The user's next screenshot (at their real 170%-zoom setup) showed it WAS broken — text overflowing section boxes and overlapping neighbors. **Fix:** switched to CSS container queries — added `container-type: inline-size` to `.canvas-scroll .newspaper-canvas`, changed `.newspaper-section strong`/`small` and `.section-label` from `vw` to `cqw` units, verified via screenshot at a viewport approximating the user's exact zoom scenario (1129×650) that overflow was fully resolved.

   - **`git add` pathspec failure (recurring mechanical issue, twice):** Running `git add <list including an already-git-rm'd path>` fails entirely with "fatal: pathspec '...' did not match any files" and stages NOTHING from that command (not even the valid paths). **Fix applied both times:** re-ran `git add` without the already-deleted path (which was already staged from the earlier `git rm`), producing two separate commits per logical change — accepted and documented as a "continuation" commit rather than treated as an error requiring a fix to git behavior itself.

   g) **The character grid (the central architectural idea)** — body must NOT be a rich editor; language a Marathi-default dropdown; no live preview but a real editor canvas (add/place/resize/crop images, remove background); then AI fills remaining space using an H/S/T/I cell map the user drew:
   ```
   H H H H H H H H H H H H
   S S S S S S S S S S S S
   T T T T T T T I I I I I

   h) **Six final items** — rotate 90° pushes the image out of the editor; text not editable in the editor; remove background not working at all; reporter story images not reaching the editor; make the layout grid 16 partitions instead of 8; and "create a newspaper by yourself by login and the ai api which we are going to send use it as a prompt to you and fill that data to check are we able to create a website or not also for images download from internet".

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Character grid / text-flow model**: one cell = one body-character wide × one line tall; images mark occupied cells; counting free `T` cells yields an exact character budget; runaround falls out of the same calculation
   - Print geometry: 330×530 mm page, 310×510 mm matter, CMYK, **2 px per mm** (→ 660×1060 px / 620×1020 px), 300 DPI print raster = 3898×6260 px
   - 16-column grid, 3 mm gutters, 4 mm baseline; blocks snap left-edge→column start, right-edge→column end
   - Fabric.js 5 (MIT, vendored) as the composition engine; **Fabric's zoom, not CSS transform** (transform breaks pointer hit-testing)
   - `getCoords()` for true rotated bounding boxes (`getBoundingRect` returns unrotated dims with a top-left origin)
   - Jimp (MIT) border flood-fill background removal + feathering + occupancy mask
   - Licence analysis: remove.bg paid; @imgly/background-removal **AGPL-3.0**; BiRefNet MIT
   - Express 4 async-handler rejections crash Node → `asyncRoute` wrapper
   - Route→Controller→Service→Repository layering; additive `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`
   - Pub/sub store with `PAGE` (structural) vs `PAGE_SYNC` (fresher rows) topics
   - Playwright (`playwright-core`) + `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, `--no-sandbox`

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   **`VISION.md`** (new) — the project constitution, verbatim from the user's document, with a precedence header. `CLAUDE.md` gained a pointer at the top saying VISION.md wins on conflict.

   **`src/layout/geometry.js`** (new) — single source of the px scale:
   ```js
   const PX_PER_MM = 2;
   const DEFAULTS = { pageWidthMm: 330, pageHeightMm: 530, matterWidthMm: 310,
     matterHeightMm: 510, bleedMm: 3, printDpi: 300, gridColumns: 16, gridGutterMm: 3 };
   // left edges and right edges kept apart so a block never starts in a gutter
   function snapPointsX(geometry) { ...; return { left, right }; }
   function typeScaleFor(widthPx, heightPx) {
     const headline = clamp(width / 11, 13, 40);
     const headlineFitted = height && height < 160 ? Math.min(headline, 18) : headline;
     return { headlineFontPx: headlineFitted,
       subheadingFontPx: clamp(headlineFitted * 0.55, 11, 22),
       bodyFontPx: clamp(width / 26, 9, 16) };
   }
   ```

   **`public/editor/layout/text-flow.js`** (new, the core) — `buildFlowMap(section, view, images)` returns `{cols, rows, cellWidth, cellHeight, grid, headlineRows, subheadingRows, imageCells, bodyCharBudget, bodyWordBudget, usedChars}`; `flowAscii()` renders the H/S/T/I map; `flowFit()`; `flowRuns(map, kind)` finds contiguous runs; `pourIntoRuns(runs, text)` breaks on spaces; `flowImageFromRow()` is the single row→flow converter. Rotation-aware:
   ```js
   function toLocal(image, cx, cy) {
     const angle = ((Number(image.rotation) || 0) * Math.PI) / 180;
     if (!angle) return { x: cx - image.x, y: cy - image.y };
     const dx = cx - image.x, dy = cy - image.y;
     const cos = Math.cos(-angle), sin = Math.sin(-angle);
     return { x: dx * cos - dy * sin, y: dx * sin + dy * cos };
   }
   ```

   **`public/editor/external-editor/fabric-surface.js`** (new) — Fabric wrapper. Critical fixes:
   ```js
   // getBoundingRect returns UNROTATED dims with a top-left origin; corners tell the truth
   function boxOf(object) {
     const corners = object.getCoords(true);
     const xs = corners.map(p => p.x), ys = corners.map(p => p.y);
     const left = Math.min(...xs), top = Math.min(...ys);
     return { left, top, width: Math.max(...xs) - left, height: Math.max(...ys) - top };
   }
   // store the picture's OWN size + angle, not the rotated box (double-counting bug)
   function placementOf(object) {
     return { x: Math.round(object.left), y: Math.round(object.top),
       width: Math.round(object.getScaledWidth()), height: Math.round(object.getScaledHeight()),
       rotation: Math.round(object.angle || 0), flipH: !!object.flipX, flipV: !!object.flipY };
   }
   // fit to column with Fabric zoom, NOT a CSS transform (transform breaks hit-testing)
   canvas.setZoom(scale); canvas.setDimensions({...}); canvas.calcOffset();
   ```
   Text objects: `selectable: true, editable: true, lockMovementX/Y: true, hasControls: false`, with an `editing:exited` handler that reassembles all pieces of a field and calls `listeners.onTextEdited(field, text)`.

   **`public/editor/external-editor/compose-canvas.js`** (rewritten) — the composition surface; `drawText` pours copy into free cells via `flowRuns`/`pourIntoRuns`; auto-selects a newly added picture; controls bar rendered **above** the canvas frame.

**Running means launching the actual app and interacting with it** —
not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a
`console.log`. The app as a user (human or programmatic) would meet
it: the CLI at its command, the server at its socket, the GUI at its
window.

## First: does a project skill already cover this?

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path —
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed
what worked: the exact `apt-get` line, the env vars, the patches, the
driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

```bash
d=$PWD; while :; do
  grep -Hm1 '^description:' "$d"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null
  [ -e "$d/.git" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break
  d=$(dirname "$d")
done
```

- **One describes launching/driving this app** → read that SKILL.md
  and follow it verbatim. Don't paraphrase; don't skip the patches.
- **Mega-repo, several plausible, no clear match** → ask the user
  which unit to run.
- **Stale** (fails on mechanics unrelated to your task) → tell the
  user; offer to refresh it via `/run-skill-generator`.
- **Nothing about running** → fall back to the patterns below.

## Otherwise: match the shape, use the pattern

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section — you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web
app, [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) — drive it with
`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) — it has the `_electron`
REPL driver skeleton and the tmux wrapping.

## Drive it, don't just launch it

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app — it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to
a point where a user would see something:

- CLI → type a representative command, check the exit code and output.
- Server → hit the route the diff touches with `curl`, read the body.
- TUI → `send-keys` a navigation, `capture-pane` the result.
- GUI → click the button, screenshot the window. **Look at the
  screenshot.** A blank frame is a failure to launch.

If the fallback pattern didn't work out of the box — you had to
install packages, set env vars, patch config, or write a driver —
recommend `/run-skill-generator` in your report so that work gets
captured as a project skill. If it just worked, don't.

     if (!container) return;

       const active = currentPage && page.id === currentPage.id;
       const filled = (page.sections || []).some((section) => section.headline);
       return `<button class="page-pill${active ? " active" : ""}${filled ? " filled" : ""}" data-page-id="${page.id}" title="Page ${page.page_number}">${page.page_number}</button>`;

     container.querySelectorAll(".page-pill").forEach((btn) => {

Second occurrence: repeated the same mistake pattern once more before self-correcting mid-session. **Fix applied and now standing practice:** always query the specific test user's `id` and match `newspapers.created_by = <that id>` (or track exact inserted IDs from setup script output) before deleting — verified via a `SELECT` first when in doubt (e.g., checking `created_by` on candidate rows before deleting).

Closing the drawer after selecting a story therefore silently reverted the populated (but unsaved) headline field to empty, causing a Playwright test timeout (`.newspaper-section.filled` never appeared because the save button's headline was blank). **Fix:** made all drawer-visibility toggles pure `classList.toggle()` DOM operations with no `render()` call, exactly matching how the sidebar behaved before it became a drawer.

   - **Lopsided ~3500px-tall page from CSS Grid stretch:** Removing `.workspace-shell`'s `height`/`overflow:hidden` entirely (to allow "some scrolling") let one long grid-row child (the 20+-item Editions list) stretch the WHOLE row height via Grid's default `align-items: stretch`, dragging the empty canvas/inspector columns down with it. **Fix:** reverted to a fixed-height (`height: calc(100vh - 60px)`), `overflow: hidden` shell, with `overflow-y: auto` scoped individually to `.sidebar-panel`, `.canvas-scroll`, and `.workspace-inspector` — "some scrolling is fine" correctly means per-panel scrolling, not whole-page scrolling.

   - **Static compact canvas width still overflowed on shorter screens:** Tried `max-width: 420px` for Fit mode first; measured via Playwright at 1366×768 that `canvasScrollHeight` (659px) still exceeded `canvasClientHeight` (587px) by ~72px — a fixed guessed width can't account for viewport-height variance. **Fix:** switched to `height: 100%; width: auto; max-width: 100%` (height-relative, CSS-computed from the actual container size) — re-measured, `scrollHeight === clientHeight` exactly, confirmed at any viewport height by construction.

   - **`vw`-relative font sizing broke down under the new layout (predicted, then confirmed):** `.newspaper-section strong` used `clamp(0.7rem, 1.6vw, 1.05rem)` — approximated the canvas's actual size only when canvas width tracked viewport width ~1:1, which stopped being true after the sidebar-drawer change (canvas became a fraction of viewport width) and again after the Fit-mode height-driven sizing. I flagged this as a predicted risk in PROJECT_STATUS.md's Follow-up 5 debt section without confirming it broken. The user's next screenshot (at their real 170%-zoom setup) showed it WAS broken — text overflowing section boxes and overlapping neighbors. **Fix:** switched to CSS container queries — added `container-type: inline-size` to `.canvas-scroll .newspaper-canvas`, changed `.newspaper-section strong`/`small` and `.section-label` from `vw` to `cqw` units, verified via screenshot at a viewport approximating the user's exact zoom scenario (1129×650) that overflow was fully resolved.

   - **`git add` pathspec failure (recurring mechanical issue, twice):** Running `git add <list including an already-git-rm'd path>` fails entirely with "fatal: pathspec '...' did not match any files" and stages NOTHING from that command (not even the valid paths). **Fix applied both times:** re-ran `git add` without the already-deleted path (which was already staged from the earlier `git rm`), producing two separate commits per logical change — accepted and documented as a "continuation" commit rather than treated as an error requiring a fix to git behavior itself.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Resolved the fundamental tension between "large canvas per the original spec" and "canvas too big causes scrolling" by reframing the canvas's job: it's a section-selector/overview, not a reading surface — full editing happens in the Inspector. This reframing (which came from the user directly) unlocked the Fit/100% toggle design and justified shrinking the default view aggressively.
   - Resolved ambiguity in "collapse the left sidebar" by initially guessing wrong (workspace's own Editions/Story-Explorer panel) and then correctly identifying, after explicit user correction, that it meant the outer app-level dashboard nav (`.sidebar`, shared across `admin.js`'s two dashboard renderers).
   - Resolved the "Editions tab" redundancy by recognizing it duplicated "Past Newspapers" (already in the outer nav, already calling `editNewspaper(id)`) — removed the duplicate rather than keeping two UIs for the same job, consistent with CLAUDE.md's stated anti-duplication principle.
   - Resolved "make Story Explorer contextual" per the user's description ("when any section is selected... after he select a story... it will close and data will auto populate") by gating the "From Reporter" toolbar button on `hasSelection` and auto-closing the picker drawer immediately after a story is clicked.
   - Resolved text legibility at small canvas sizes using CSS container queries instead of viewport units — a durable, zoom-level-and-mode-independent solution rather than another guessed constant.
   - No unresolved/ongoing troubleshooting at the point of this summary — the last commit (`2582c49`) passed all verification (16/16 tests, Playwright screenshots at two viewport sizes, zero console/page errors) and the working tree is clean except pre-existing untracked `.png` upload artifacts unrelated to this work.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Character grid / text-flow**: one cell = one body-character wide × one line tall; H/S/T/I map; free `T` cells = exact character budget; runaround falls out of the same calculation
   - **MIN_LINE_HEIGHT = 1.45** — Devanagari stacks vowel signs above the shirorekha (ि े ै ो ं) and below the baseline (ु ृ); a 1.25 line box crops them
   - Print geometry: 330×530 mm page, 310×510 mm matter, CMYK, **2 px/mm** → 660×1060 px page / 620×1020 px matter; 16 columns, 3 mm gutters, 4 mm baseline
   - **Four categories of ink**: standing furniture (never changes) / edition variables (daily but *derivable*) / **standing daily features** (daily, no reporter) / the day's file
   - Feature source classification: **computed** (free, offline, cannot be wrong) / **curated** (person-checked once) / **written** (one AI call for all) / **feed** (must not be invented)
   - U²-Net (Apache-2.0) via onnxruntime-node (MIT); @imgly is AGPL-3.0 (unusable), remove.bg is paid
   - Sunrise equation (NOAA), rahukaal = 1/8th of daylight by weekday, Shaka year rollover at Chaitra 1 (21/22 March)
   - Verso/recto: page number on the OUTER edge — left on even pages, right on odd
   - Colour formes: outer forme (first two + last two pages) + centre spread
   - Column-centimetre advert pricing; position dominates price
   - Scribus `.sla` XML (PTYPE 4 = text frame, PTYPE 2 = image, TEXTFLOWMODE 2 = runaround)

not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path —
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed
what worked: the exact `apt-get` line, the env vars, the patches, the
driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

```bash
d=$PWD; while :; do
  grep -Hm1 '^description:' "$d"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null
  [ -e "$d/.git" ] || [ "$d" = / ] && break
  d=$(dirname "$d")
done
```

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section — you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web
app, [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) — drive it with
`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) — it has the `_electron`
REPL driver skeleton and the tmux wrapping.

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app — it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to

- CMYK/PDF production
- advanced paragraph composition
- production-quality print output

Objectives

1. Remove the current vertically scrolling interface.

3. Preserve all existing backend APIs.

4. Preserve all business logic.

5. Preserve the current modular architecture.

6. Only reorganize the UI architecture.

Workspace Layout

------------------------------------------------------------

Top Toolbar

- Save
- Undo
- Redo
- Preview
- Export
- AI
- Publish

------------------------------------------------------------

Left Sidebar

- Editions
- Pages
- Story Explorer
- Search
- Filters
- Reporter Stories

Center

Large Newspaper Workspace

Right Sidebar

Context Inspector

- metadata
- article information
- typography
- image information
- section properties

------------------------------------------------------------

Bottom

Page Navigator

Support newspapers containing dozens of pages.

------------------------------------------------------------

The workspace must comfortably support:

- 10–50 editorial sections on one page
- 24+ pages in one edition
- thousands of reporter stories
- future AI features
- future image editing
- future production layout engine integration

   This conversation covers a single large iterative task: redesigning the SAHAS Newspaper Workspace (`public/editor/*.js` + `public/styles.css` + supporting `public/admin.js` changes), driven through multiple rounds of user feedback after each visible result. In chronological order, the user's explicit requests were:

   a) **Initial architectural redesign request** (verbatim excerpt): "Before implementing any new editor features, redesign the SAHAS Newspaper Workspace... This is NOT a visual redesign. This is an architectural redesign... Remember that SAHAS will later integrate an external professional layout editor... Therefore DO NOT redesign the editor to become another InDesign. Instead build the workspace that will HOST those capabilities." Specified exact regions: Top Toolbar (Save/Undo/Redo/Preview/Export/AI/Publish), Left Sidebar (Editions/Pages/Story Explorer/Search/Filters/Reporter Stories), Center (large canvas, 70-80% of screen), Right Sidebar (Context Inspector: metadata/article info/typography/image info/section properties), Bottom (Page Navigator with thumbnails, support 24+ pages). Explicitly forbade implementing crop/typography-engine/text-wrapping/drag-drop improvements. Required: review architecture → explain proposed architecture → explain why it scales → then implement. Required after: update PROJECT_STATUS.md, run full test suite, Playwright smoke test, commit only after tests pass.

   b) **Visual feedback round 1** (verbatim, with screenshot at 170% browser zoom): "NOT User friendly also looking UI is very conjested and ugly some scrolling full page is acceptable. Design it like a Newpaper editor will use it everyday."

   c) **Visual feedback round 2** (verbatim, with a screenshot showing a ~3500px-tall lopsided page): "Even after that I dont think so this is a even a good UI ,I want a great UI"

   d) **Visual feedback round 3** (verbatim, with a screenshot plus 3 hand-drawn notebook wireframe photos): "this is a long screenshot , I think what you can to left side bar into one button in top with 3 bars horizontal (Increase space), small layout showing at bottem remove it and make big layout (which) is in middle to top right corner with appropriate length to able to select are, I created a MVP for you in my notebook and upload image for you understand the image then implement"

   e) **Correction to (d)** (verbatim): "I think you put wrong things in button(button in top with 3 bars horizontal) I want to move past newspapar,past news,reporter,settings,logout in that button and edition and story explorer -> put a button on top when any section in layout is selected from reporter and then right bar will show them both after he select a story/news/edition and save it will close and data will auto populate in right side bar ALSO if you have any better idea suggest me"

   f) **Visual feedback round 4** (verbatim, with screenshot): "Yes this is fine but not great. If you look layout in middel it is too big to fit in laptop screen I need to do lot scorlling , I just need to select (news section/editorial section) in the layout as full will show in below with external editor so we can make layout some small also if you have a good idea implement that too"

   g) **Most recent feedback round 5** (verbatim, with screenshot at 170% zoom showing overflowing text): "the text is overflowing also we can make right side bar bigger to take input it will visually good also"

   Throughout, the standing constraints from the original task carried forward: preserve backend APIs, preserve business logic, preserve modular architecture, run `npm test` + Playwright smoke test before every commit, update PROJECT_STATUS.md after each change, only commit when tests pass.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - CSS Grid layout for the workspace shell (`grid-template-areas`/`grid-template-columns`/`grid-template-rows`), and the specific failure mode where a long unbounded child in one grid row stretches the whole row height via default `align-items: stretch`.
   - Fixed-position "drawer" UI pattern (`position: fixed; transform: translateX(-100%); transition: transform 0.2s ease;` + `.open` class + backdrop overlay with click-to-close), reused consistently across: the Publish modal, the workspace's own former Editions/Story-Explorer drawer, the current contextual Story Picker drawer, and the outer app-level `.sidebar` drawer.
   - CSS Container Queries (`container-type: inline-size` + `cqw` units) as the fix for text that must scale with a shrinking/resizing parent element rather than the browser viewport (`vw` units) — critical fix in the final commit.
   - Height-relative vs. width-relative sizing for a fixed-aspect-ratio box (`aspect-ratio` CSS property set inline per-newspaper in `canvas.js`) — realized a static guessed pixel width cannot guarantee "fits without scrolling" across different viewport heights; only container-relative/height-relative sizing can.
   - One-directional data flow architecture established in earlier sessions: `workspace.js` owns all state in a single module-scoped `state` object; child modules (`toolbar.js`, `story-picker.js`, `canvas.js`, `layout-sidebar.js`, `inspector.js`, `page-navigator.js`) receive data/callbacks as function arguments and never import each other directly.
   - The specific bug pattern of calling a full `render()` (which rebuilds all DOM from `state`) when only a DOM-only, out-of-`state` mutation (like `applyStoryToInspector`, which directly sets `<input>` values) needs to be preserved — fixed by making UI-only toggles (drawer open/close) pure `classList.toggle()` operations instead.
   - Playwright (`playwright-core`) browser automation for smoke testing, installed fresh each session in a scratchpad directory (`/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/browsertest/`) since it doesn't persist between sessions, pointed at system Chrome (`/usr/bin/google-chrome`).
   - Test-data hygiene discipline: **always clean up test fixtures (temp users, seeded news_items, newspapers) using exact IDs or `created_by` matching — never a time-window (`created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL`) query**, established as a hard rule after two separate incidents where a broad time-window delete removed unrelated rows (disclosed transparently to the user both times).
   - `git add` with a mix of real file paths and one already-deleted (via `git rm`) path fails entirely with "fatal: pathspec ... did not match any files" — requires splitting into two separate commits (the deletion, staged from `git rm`, commits alone first; a follow-up commit picks up the rest).

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **`public/editor/workspace.js`** — central orchestrator, rewritten multiple times this session. Final state (as of last commit `2582c49`, though that commit didn't touch this file — last modified in the Fit/100% toggle commit `27a8b07`):
   ```js
   const state = {
     newspaper: null,
     pages: [],
     currentPage: null,
     reporterNews: [],
     selectedSection: null,
     storyPickerOpen: false,
     canvasZoom: "fit",
   };
   ```
   Key functions: `renderWorkspace(newspaperId)` (fetches newspaper/pages/reporterNews, resets `selectedSection`/`storyPickerOpen`, calls `render()`), `selectPage`, `selectSection`, `applyTemplate`, `saveSection` (all full `render()` calls, appropriate since they mutate real state), `applyStoryPickerVisibility()`/`toggleStoryPicker()`/`closeStoryPicker()` (pure DOM `classList.toggle`, NO `render()` — this was the critical bug fix), `selectStoryForSection(story)` (calls `applyStoryToInspector(story)` then `closeStoryPicker()`), `setZoom(mode)`/`renderZoomToggle()` (local, DOM-only, no new file), `triggerSave()`, `openPublish()`. The `render()` function builds the shell markup:
   ```js
   content.innerHTML = `
     <div class="workspace-shell">
       <header class="workspace-toolbar" id="toolbar"></header>
       <div class="workspace-body">
         <div class="sidebar-backdrop${state.storyPickerOpen ? " open" : ""}" id="sidebarBackdrop"></div>
         <aside class="workspace-sidebar-left${state.storyPickerOpen ? " open" : ""}" id="sidebarLeft">
           <div class="sidebar-drawer-header">
             <h3>Story Explorer</h3>
             <button class="sidebar-drawer-close" id="sidebarDrawerClose">&times;</button>
           </div>

           <div class="canvas-toolbar">

             <div class="canvas-toolbar-spacer"></div>
             <div id="zoomToggle" class="zoom-toggle"></div>
           </div>

   Imports: `renderCanvas` from `canvas.js`, `renderPageNavigator` from `page-navigator.js`, `renderLayoutSidebar` from `layout-sidebar.js`, `renderInspector, applyStoryToInspector` from `inspector.js`, `renderStoryPicker` from `story-picker.js`, `renderToolbar` from `toolbar.js`, `showPublicationFiles` from `publication.js`.

   **`public/editor/toolbar.js`** — icon-based toolbar. `ICONS` object with hand-written inline SVGs (`search`, `save`, `undo`, `redo`, `preview`, `export`, `ai`, `publish`). `button(id, icon, label, {disabled, primary, active, title})` helper. `renderToolbar({newspaper, hasSelection, storyPickerOpen, onSave, onPublish, onToggleStoryPicker})` renders `.toolbar-left` (brand name/date only, no hamburger anymore) and `.toolbar-actions` starting with "From Reporter" (`id="tbFromReporter"`, disabled unless `hasSelection`, `active` class when `storyPickerOpen`), then Save/Undo/Redo/Preview/Export/AI/Publish.

   **`public/editor/story-picker.js`** (new, replaces deleted `sidebar-left.js`):
   ```js
   import { renderStoryExplorerMarkup, bindStoryExplorer } from "./story-explorer.js";
   export function renderStoryPicker(currentPage, reporterNews, selectedSectionKey, onSelectStory) {
     const panel = document.getElementById("sidebarPanel");
     if (!panel) return;
     const section = currentPage?.sections?.find((s) => s.section_key === selectedSectionKey);
     panel.innerHTML = renderStoryExplorerMarkup(reporterNews);
     bindStoryExplorer(reporterNews, onSelectStory, section?.news_item_id || null);
   }
   ```

   **`public/editor/page-navigator.js`** — rewritten twice: first from thumbnail-based bottom strip to compact "page-pill" buttons in the top canvas-toolbar strip:
   ```js
   export function renderPageNavigator(pages, currentPage, newspaper, onSelectPage) {
     const container = document.getElementById("pageSwitcher");
     if (!container) return;
     container.innerHTML = pages.map((page) => {
       const active = currentPage && page.id === currentPage.id;
       const filled = (page.sections || []).some((section) => section.headline);
       return `<button class="page-pill${active ? " active" : ""}${filled ? " filled" : ""}" data-page-id="${page.id}" title="Page ${page.page_number}">${page.page_number}</button>`;
     }).join("");
     container.querySelectorAll(".page-pill").forEach((btn) => {
       btn.addEventListener("click", () => onSelectPage(Number(btn.dataset.pageId)));
     });
   }
   ```
   No longer imports `canvas-geometry.js` (dropped the mini live-thumbnail rendering).

   **`public/editor/canvas.js`** — imports `sectionRect` from `canvas-geometry.js`, renders `.newspaper-canvas` with inline `aspect-ratio:${pageWidth}/${pageHeight}` style. Unchanged in the most recent commits (only CSS around it changed).

   **`public/editor/canvas-geometry.js`** — `export function sectionRect(section, pageWidth, pageHeight)` returning `{leftPct, topPct, widthPct, heightPct}`. Still used by `canvas.js` only (as of the pill-based page-navigator rewrite).

   **`public/admin.js`** — modified to add app-level sidebar drawer:
   ```js
   function toggleAppSidebar() {
     document.querySelector(".sidebar")?.classList.toggle("open");
     document.querySelector(".sidebar-app-backdrop")?.classList.toggle("open");
   }
   function closeAppSidebar() {
     document.querySelector(".sidebar")?.classList.remove("open");
     document.querySelector(".sidebar-app-backdrop")?.classList.remove("open");
   }
   function wireAppSidebarToggle() {
     document.getElementById("appSidebarToggle").addEventListener("click", toggleAppSidebar);
     document.getElementById("sidebarAppBackdrop").addEventListener("click", closeAppSidebar);
     document.querySelector(".sidebar").addEventListener("click", (event) => {
       if (event.target.classList.contains("sidebar-btn")) closeAppSidebar();
     });
   }
   ```
   Both `renderReporterDashboard()` and `renderAdminDashboard()` markup updated with `<button class="hamburger-btn" id="appSidebarToggle" title="Menu">&#9776;</button>` inside `.header-left`, and `<div class="sidebar-app-backdrop" id="sidebarAppBackdrop"></div>` inside `.container`, plus a `wireAppSidebarToggle();` call after each `app.innerHTML` assignment. `editNewspaper()` now also calls `closeAppSidebar();`.

4. Errors and fixes:

   - **Cleanup query too broad (occurred twice):** First occurrence used `created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '2 hours'` and deleted 27 unrelated newspaper rows (including 2 with `status: 'finalised'`) instead of just the test's own row. Disclosed transparently to the user in the next response. Second occurrence: repeated the same mistake pattern once more before self-correcting mid-session. **Fix applied and now standing practice:** always query the specific test user's `id` and match `newspapers.created_by = <that id>` (or track exact inserted IDs from setup script output) before deleting — verified via a `SELECT` first when in doubt (e.g., checking `created_by` on candidate rows before deleting).

   - **Drawer toggle wiped unsaved inspector data:** The first implementation of `toggleSidebar()`/`closeSidebar()` (later renamed `toggleStoryPicker`/`closeStoryPicker`) called the shared `render()` function, which rebuilds the Inspector from `state` — but `applyStoryToInspector()` populates `<input>` values by direct DOM mutation, bypassing `state` entirely. Closing the drawer after selecting a story therefore silently reverted the populated (but unsaved) headline field to empty, causing a Playwright test timeout (`.newspaper-section.filled` never appeared because the save button's headline was blank). **Fix:** made all drawer-visibility toggles pure `classList.toggle()` DOM operations with no `render()` call, exactly matching how the sidebar behaved before it became a drawer.

   - **Lopsided ~3500px-tall page from CSS Grid stretch:** Removing `.workspace-shell`'s `height`/`overflow:hidden` entirely (to allow "some scrolling") let one long grid-row child (the 20+-item Editions list) stretch the WHOLE row height via Grid's default `align-items: stretch`, dragging the empty canvas/inspector columns down with it. **Fix:** reverted to a fixed-height (`height: calc(100vh - 60px)`), `overflow: hidden` shell, with `overflow-y: auto` scoped individually to `.sidebar-panel`, `.canvas-scroll`, and `.workspace-inspector` — "some scrolling is fine" correctly means per-panel scrolling, not whole-page scrolling.

   - **Static compact canvas width still overflowed on shorter screens:** Tried `max-width: 420px` for Fit mode first; measured via Playwright at 1366×768 that `canvasScrollHeight` (659px) still exceeded `canvasClientHeight` (587px) by ~72px — a fixed guessed width can't account for viewport-height variance. **Fix:** switched to `height: 100%; width: auto; max-width: 100%` (height-relative, CSS-computed from the actual container size) — re-measured, `scrollHeight === clientHeight` exactly, confirmed at any viewport height by construction.

   - **`vw`-relative font sizing broke down under the new layout (predicted, then confirmed):** `.newspaper-section strong` used `clamp(0.7rem, 1.6vw, 1.05rem)` — approximated the canvas's actual size only when canvas width tracked viewport width ~1:1, which stopped being true after the sidebar-drawer change (canvas became a fraction of viewport width) and again after the Fit-mode height-driven sizing. I flagged this as a predicted risk in PROJECT_STATUS.md's Follow-up 5 debt section without confirming it broken. The user's next screenshot (at their real 170%-zoom setup) showed it WAS broken — text overflowing section boxes and overlapping neighbors. **Fix:** switched to CSS container queries — added `container-type: inline-size` to `.canvas-scroll .newspaper-canvas`, changed `.newspaper-section strong`/`small` and `.section-label` from `vw` to `cqw` units, verified via screenshot at a viewport approximating the user's exact zoom scenario (1129×650) that overflow was fully resolved.

   - **`git add` pathspec failure (recurring mechanical issue, twice):** Running `git add <list including an already-git-rm'd path>` fails entirely with "fatal: pathspec '...' did not match any files" and stages NOTHING from that command (not even the valid paths). **Fix applied both times:** re-ran `git add` without the already-deleted path (which was already staged from the earlier `git rm`), producing two separate commits per logical change — accepted and documented as a "continuation" commit rather than treated as an error requiring a fix to git behavior itself.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Resolved the fundamental tension between "large canvas per the original spec" and "canvas too big causes scrolling" by reframing the canvas's job: it's a section-selector/overview, not a reading surface — full editing happens in the Inspector. This reframing (which came from the user directly) unlocked the Fit/100% toggle design and justified shrinking the default view aggressively.
   - Resolved ambiguity in "collapse the left sidebar" by initially guessing wrong (workspace's own Editions/Story-Explorer panel) and then correctly identifying, after explicit user correction, that it meant the outer app-level dashboard nav (`.sidebar`, shared across `admin.js`'s two dashboard renderers).
   - Resolved the "Editions tab" redundancy by recognizing it duplicated "Past Newspapers" (already in the outer nav, already calling `editNewspaper(id)`) — removed the duplicate rather than keeping two UIs for the same job, consistent with CLAUDE.md's stated anti-duplication principle.
   - Resolved "make Story Explorer contextual" per the user's description ("when any section is selected... after he select a story... it will close and data will auto populate") by gating the "From Reporter" toolbar button on `hasSelection` and auto-closing the picker drawer immediately after a story is clicked.
   - Resolved text legibility at small canvas sizes using CSS container queries instead of viewport units — a durable, zoom-level-and-mode-independent solution rather than another guessed constant.
   - No unresolved/ongoing troubleshooting at the point of this summary — the last commit (`2582c49`) passed all verification (16/16 tests, Playwright screenshots at two viewport sizes, zero console/page errors) and the working tree is clean except pre-existing untracked `.png` upload artifacts unrelated to this work.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - CSS Grid `grid-template-areas` / `grid-template-columns` with `minmax()` for shell layout
   - CSS custom properties (`--inspector-width`, `--canvas-height`) driven by drag splitters, persisted to localStorage
   - CSS Container Queries (`container-type: inline-size` + `cqw` units) for canvas text that scales with the container, not the viewport
   - Whole-page (document-flow) scrolling vs. fixed `100vh` app-shell with `overflow: hidden`
   - `position: sticky` for the toolbar; the failure mode of `position: sticky; bottom: 0` in a panel taller than the viewport (it pins and floats over content)
   - CSS Grid items default to `min-width: auto` and therefore never shrink — requires `minmax(0, 1fr)` + `min-width: 0`
   - Pub/sub store with named topics for surgical re-rendering (`TOPICS.DRAFT`, `PAGE`, `PAGE_SYNC`, `SELECTION`, `SAVE`, `STORY_PICKER`, `ZOOM`, `HISTORY`)
   - `source` threading through draft updates so a panel ignores the echo of its own edit (prevents caret jumping)
   - MutationObserver-based empirical performance verification
   - Real `scale()` transform for canvas zoom (preserves proportions) vs. width-based zoom tricks
   - Cursor-anchored zoom math: `panX = anchor.x - ratio * (anchor.x - panX)`
   - Additive schema migrations via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (documented CLAUDE.md pattern)
   - Route→Controller→Service→Repository layering (already implemented for news/newspapers/pages/pageSections)
   - Playwright (`playwright-core`) + system Chrome at `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, `--no-sandbox`
   - `page.route()` as a write-guard to make a tour of real customer data provably read-only
   - `onerror` inline handlers for graceful image fallback

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   **`public/editor/store.js`** (new, ~180 lines) — single source of truth. Topics include the critical split:
   ```js
   export const TOPICS = {
     EDITION: "edition",
     PAGE: "page",          // structural change (switched page, new template)
     PAGE_SYNC: "pageSync", // same page, fresher rows - e.g. what a save returned
     SELECTION: "selection",
     DRAFT: "draft",
     SAVE: "save",
     HISTORY: "history",
     STORY_PICKER: "storyPicker",
     ZOOM: "zoom",
   };
   export function replacePage(page, { structural = false } = {}) {
     state.pages = state.pages.map((p) => (p.id === page.id ? page : p));
     emit(structural ? TOPICS.PAGE : TOPICS.PAGE_SYNC);
   }
   export function updateDraft(patch, source = null) { ... emit(TOPICS.DRAFT, { patch, changed, source }); emit(TOPICS.SAVE); }
   ```

   **`public/editor/section-model.js`** (new, ~159 lines) — the only place the three shapes (DB row / camelCase draft / PUT payload) are converted. `draftFromSection`, `draftFromStory`, `payloadFromDraft`, `viewOfSection`.

   **`public/editor/status/section-status.js`** (new) — lifecycle. Key fix:

   export const CONTENT_FIELDS = ["headline", "subheading", "body", "caption", "imageUrl"];
   export function isContentEdit(patch) { return Object.keys(patch).some((key) => CONTENT_FIELDS.includes(key)); }
   export function statusOf(view) {
     if (isExplicit(view.status)) return view.status;
     if (view.aiGenerated) return "ai_generated";
     if (!view.headline && !view.body && !view.imageUrl) return view.newsItemId ? "story_linked" : "empty";
     if (view.status === "editing") return "editing";
     return view.newsItemId ? "story_linked" : "editing";
   }

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Character grid / text-flow model**: one cell = one body-character wide × one line tall; images mark occupied cells; counting free `T` cells yields an exact character budget; runaround falls out of the same calculation
   - Print geometry: 330×530 mm page, 310×510 mm matter, CMYK, **2 px per mm** (→ 660×1060 px / 620×1020 px), 300 DPI print raster = 3898×6260 px
   - 16-column grid, 3 mm gutters, 4 mm baseline; blocks snap left-edge→column start, right-edge→column end
   - Fabric.js 5 (MIT, vendored) as the composition engine; **Fabric's zoom, not CSS transform** (transform breaks pointer hit-testing)
   - `getCoords()` for true rotated bounding boxes (`getBoundingRect` returns unrotated dims with a top-left origin)

   **`public/editor/layout/text-flow.js`** (new, the core) — `buildFlowMap(section, view, images)` returns `{cols, rows, cellWidth, cellHeight, grid, headlineRows, subheadingRows, imageCells, bodyCharBudget, bodyWordBudget, usedChars}`; `flowAscii()` renders the H/S/T/I map; `flowFit()`; `flowRuns(map, kind)` finds contiguous runs; `pourIntoRuns(runs, text)` breaks on spaces; `flowImageFromRow()` is the single row→flow converter. Rotation-aware:
   ```js
   function toLocal(image, cx, cy) {
     const angle = ((Number(image.rotation) || 0) * Math.PI) / 180;
     if (!angle) return { x: cx - image.x, y: cy - image.y };
     const dx = cx - image.x, dy = cy - image.y;
     const cos = Math.cos(-angle), sin = Math.sin(-angle);
     return { x: dx * cos - dy * sin, y: dx * sin + dy * cos };
   }
   ```

   **`public/editor/external-editor/fabric-surface.js`** (new) — Fabric wrapper. Critical fixes:
   ```js
   // getBoundingRect returns UNROTATED dims with a top-left origin; corners tell the truth
   function boxOf(object) {
     const corners = object.getCoords(true);
     const xs = corners.map(p => p.x), ys = corners.map(p => p.y);
     const left = Math.min(...xs), top = Math.min(...ys);
     return { left, top, width: Math.max(...xs) - left, height: Math.max(...ys) - top };
   }
   // store the picture's OWN size + angle, not the rotated box (double-counting bug)
   function placementOf(object) {
     return { x: Math.round(object.left), y: Math.round(object.top),
       width: Math.round(object.getScaledWidth()), height: Math.round(object.getScaledHeight()),
       rotation: Math.round(object.angle || 0), flipH: !!object.flipX, flipV: !!object.flipY };
   }
   // fit to column with Fabric zoom, NOT a CSS transform (transform breaks hit-testing)
   canvas.setZoom(scale); canvas.setDimensions({...}); canvas.calcOffset();

   - **Markup is presentation, text is content** — everything that measures reads plain text; everything that renders reads the marks. One module (`rich-text.js`) for browser and server.
   - **`max_tokens` is a CEILING, not a spend** — providers bill tokens produced; a lower ceiling saves nothing and risks an empty response you already paid reasoning for.
   - **CSS specificity:** two rules of equal specificity — the later one wins. An override declared *above* a base rule does nothing.
   - **`display: flex` beats the `hidden` attribute**; `min-width: 0` is required because a flex item's automatic minimum size is its *content* size; a `<select>` is sized by its **longest option**, not its box.
   - **`position: sticky` is only correct when there is something *beside* the pinned element to scroll** — a sticky element paints above in-flow content beneath it.

       const height = Number(row.height_px) / scale;

       const quarter = turn % 180 !== 0;
       const frame = [`left:${Number(row.x_px)/scale}px`, `top:${Number(row.y_px)/scale}px`,

# PHASE 4 — FIX THE AI DOUBLE-CALL / FIT BUDGET BUG

We are continuing from commit:

b128b56 — A used-up quota and a busy minute are both 429

- npm tests: 201/201

- no secrets leaked
- Gemini browser E2E is still NOT VERIFIED because quota was exhausted

The most important unresolved issue is this:

A normal "Write this block" currently often makes TWO AI calls.

This is not because the first AI response is necessarily bad.

The deeper problem is:

1. planningFit() reserves space using a MAXIMUM headline/deck placeholder
2. AI writes an actual headline/deck that is often shorter
3. the actual available body space is therefore larger than the space originally given to the model
4. the model correctly writes to the smaller budget it was given
5. the application measures the result against the larger real budget
6. it thinks the story is too short
7. it makes a second AI call

In one real edition:

32 of 34 article blocks would trigger the repair pass.

Examples:

lead:
briefed = 192
judged = 315

anchor:
briefed = 384
judged = 528

report-two:
briefed = 95
judged = 19

So the current system can tell the model:

"Write between 177 and 192 characters"

and then judge it against:

"315 characters available."

That is logically inconsistent.

DO NOT simply increase the first prompt's budget.

We need to fix the measurement relationship.

============================================================
PART 1 — UNDERSTAND THE CURRENT FLOW
============================================================

Before modifying anything, inspect:

src/services/storyWriter.service.js

Specifically:

measure()
planningFit()
briefFor()
write()
resizeBriefFor()

Trace the exact values through:

empty block
→ planningFit
→ first AI request
→ returned headline
→ returned subheading
→ real measure
→ resize decision

Do this with instrumentation/tests, not assumptions.

Create a deterministic test/harness if necessary.

Do not call real AI while investigating.

============================================================
PART 2 — DEFINE THE CORRECT FIT MODEL
============================================================

     export function placedPictureStyle(row, scale = 1) {
       const width = Number(row.width_px) / scale;
       const height = Number(row.height_px) / scale;
       const turn = (((Number(row.rotation) || 0) % 360) + 360) % 360;
       const quarter = turn % 180 !== 0;
       const frame = [`left:${Number(row.x_px)/scale}px`, `top:${Number(row.y_px)/scale}px`,
                      `width:${width}px`, `height:${height}px`, `z-index:${Number(row.z_index)||1}`].join(";");
       const image = ["position:absolute","left:50%","top:50%",
         `width:${quarter ? height : width}px`, `height:${quarter ? width : height}px`,
         "object-fit:contain",
         `transform:translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(${turn}deg)` + (row.flip_h ? " scaleX(-1)" : "") + (row.flip_v ? " scaleY(-1)" : ""),
         row.shape === "ellipse" ? "border-radius:50%" : ""].filter(Boolean).join(";");
       return { frame, image, shape: row.shape || "rect" };
     }
     ```

   - **The character grid** (`public/editor/layout/text-flow.js`) — one cell = one body-character wide × one line tall; `CELL = {HEADLINE:'H', SUBHEADING:'S', TEXT:'T', IMAGE:'I', EMPTY:'.'}`; free `T` cells = exact character budget. `MIN_LINE_HEIGHT = 1.45` for Devanagari. Imported by the server via dynamic `import()`. Single source of measurement for worklist, fit, jump, preflight, AI brief.
   - **Print geometry:** 330×530 mm page, 2 px/mm → 660×1060 px; blocks stored in "block pixels".
   - **CSS floats can only touch the left or right edge of a column** — this is why text cannot wrap around an arbitrarily placed image, and no editor library (Quill/TipTap/CKEditor) changes it since they all render through the same engine. This was the central realization.
   - **The DTP/frames model** (InDesign/Canva/Scribus) — a page at true proportions with independently placed frames; adopted as "Option A".
   - **Quill 2.0.3** vendored at `public/vendor/quill/` (BSD-3-Clause — permissive, unlike the AGPL background-removal library the project rejected). No bundler; loaded via injected `<script>`/`<link>`.
   - **CSS specificity trap:** two rules of equal specificity — the later one wins. An override declared *above* a base rule does nothing. Hit twice this session.
   - **Jimp cannot decode WEBP** — `Mime type image/webp does not support decoding`. Browsers can, so conversion happens client-side.
   - **`object-fit: cover` vs `contain`** — cover crops; a placement carrying the picture's own proportions has nothing to crop.
   - **markup is presentation, text is content** (`rich-text.js`) — everything that measures reads `plainText()`.
   - Regression net method: baseline run → change → re-run → report the delta.

     export function placedPictureStyle(row, scale = 1) {
       const width = Number(row.width_px) / scale;
       const height = Number(row.height_px) / scale;
       const turn = (((Number(row.rotation) || 0) % 360) + 360) % 360;
       const quarter = turn % 180 !== 0;
       const frame = [`left:${Number(row.x_px)/scale}px`, `top:${Number(row.y_px)/scale}px`,
                      `width:${width}px`, `height:${height}px`, `z-index:${Number(row.z_index)||1}`].join(";");
       const image = ["position:absolute","left:50%","top:50%",
         `width:${quarter ? height : width}px`, `height:${quarter ? width : height}px`,
         "object-fit:contain",
         `transform:translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(${turn}deg)` + (row.flip_h ? " scaleX(-1)" : "") + (row.flip_v ? " scaleY(-1)" : ""),
         row.shape === "ellipse" ? "border-radius:50%" : ""].filter(Boolean).join(";");
       return { frame, image, shape: row.shape || "rect" };
     }
     ```

# PHASE 4 — FIX THE AI DOUBLE-CALL / FIT BUDGET BUG

We are continuing from commit:

b128b56 — A used-up quota and a busy minute are both 429

The previous hardening phase is complete.

Confirmed baseline:

- npm tests: 201/201
- browser tests: 49/49
- tree was clean
- AI_PROVIDER=gemini
- AI_FALLBACK_PROVIDER=sarvam,anthropic
- Gemini primary
- Sarvam fallback
- Anthropic final fallback
- provider failures are classified
- quota failures do not retry the same provider
- outputExhausted can retry
- Smart Card malformed JSON cannot crash the renderer
- editor sees useful fallback messages
- no secrets leaked
- Gemini browser E2E is still NOT VERIFIED because quota was exhausted

The most important unresolved issue is this:

A normal "Write this block" currently often makes TWO AI calls.

This is not because the first AI response is necessarily bad.

The deeper problem is:

1. planningFit() reserves space using a MAXIMUM headline/deck placeholder
2. AI writes an actual headline/deck that is often shorter
3. the actual available body space is therefore larger than the space originally given to the model
4. the model correctly writes to the smaller budget it was given
5. the application measures the result against the larger real budget
6. it thinks the story is too short
7. it makes a second AI call

In one real edition:

32 of 34 article blocks would trigger the repair pass.

Examples:

lead:
briefed = 192
judged = 315

anchor:
briefed = 384
judged = 528

report-two:
briefed = 95
judged = 19

So the current system can tell the model:

"Write between 177 and 192 characters"

and then judge it against:

"315 characters available."

That is logically inconsistent.

DO NOT simply increase the first prompt's budget.

We need to fix the measurement relationship.

============================================================
PART 1 — UNDERSTAND THE CURRENT FLOW
============================================================

Before modifying anything, inspect:

src/services/storyWriter.service.js

Specifically:

measure()
planningFit()
briefFor()
write()
resizeBriefFor()

Trace the exact values through:

empty block
→ planningFit
→ first AI request
→ returned headline
→ returned subheading
→ real measure
→ resize decision

Do this with instrumentation/tests, not assumptions.

Create a deterministic test/harness if necessary.

Do not call real AI while investigating.

============================================================
PART 2 — DEFINE THE CORRECT FIT MODEL
============================================================

We need ONE consistent concept:

The first AI request should be given a body budget that is reasonably representative of the space available after the headline and subheading it is actually going to write.

But we cannot know the exact headline before generation.

Therefore we need a practical strategy.

Evaluate these options:

A. Reserve maximum headline/deck
B. Reserve typical/expected headline/deck
C. Generate headline/deck first, then body
D. Generate everything once and accept a reasonable tolerance
E. Generate everything once, measure actual fit, and only repair when genuinely necessary
F. Tier-dependent behavior

Do NOT immediately implement C.

It would create another model call unless headline/deck generation is somehow incorporated differently.

I want the simplest solution that preserves:

- newspaper layout quality
- fact safety
- one-click workflow
- minimal AI calls
- predictable behavior

============================================================
PART 3 — IMPLEMENT OPTION C AS THE DEFAULT DECISION RULE
============================================================

The first improvement should be:

DO NOT trigger the second call merely because the first answer is below 90% of the newly measured budget if the difference is caused by the planned-vs-real headline reservation.

Instead distinguish:

1. genuine underfill
2. measurement difference caused by headline/deck reservation

For example:

If:

planned budget = 192
actual available budget = 315
AI body = 190

then the model followed its instructions.

This should NOT automatically trigger a repair.

If:

planned budget = 192
actual available budget = 315
AI body = 90

then the story is genuinely short.

A repair may be justified.

We need a principled rule.

Do not use arbitrary magic numbers without testing.

============================================================
PART 4 — PRESERVE OVERFLOW REPAIR
============================================================

Overflow is different.

Example:

planned budget = 315
actual budget = 315
AI body = 360

This genuinely does not fit.

A repair is appropriate.

Do not accidentally remove overflow correction.

Similarly:

actual available = 315
body = 305

This is already a good fit.

Do not call AI again.

============================================================
PART 5 — DESIGN THE ACCEPTABLE FIT RANGE
============================================================

We need to establish an actual acceptance rule.

The current rule is effectively:

body < 90% → repair
body > 100% → repair

Evaluate whether this should become something like:

body within acceptable range → accept
body substantially underfilled → repair
body overflowing → repair

But the threshold must account for the fact that:

- newspaper layout is character-grid based
- exact character count is not equivalent to visual density
- Marathi characters have Unicode code-unit considerations
- paragraph breaks affect flow
- headline length affects available body space
- pictures affect available body space

Do not optimize purely around percentages.

Use the actual text-flow module wherever possible.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Provider-neutral router pattern**: `src/services/information/index.js` mirrors `src/services/ai/index.js`'s shape (isConfigured/status/fetchContext vs isConfigured/status/askForJson), with `PROVIDERS = { rss }` analogous to `ai.PROVIDERS`.
