# BUG 2 — PARAGRAPH SPACING IS CARRIED ACROSS COLUMNS USING THE OLD COLUMN'S ABSOLUTE Y

Current forced-paragraph code approximately computes:

```js
const nextY =
  lastLine.y
  + lastLine.height
  + paragraphSpacingPx;
```

and then advances the current cursor until:

```js
cursor.y >= nextY
```

That is correct only when the next paragraph continues in the **same column**.

It is wrong when the previous paragraph ends at the bottom of column 1 and the new paragraph must start in column 2.

Current behavior can become:

```text
paragraph 1 ends near y=228 in column 1
paragraphSpacingPx = 8
↓
column 1 has no room
↓
move to column 2
↓
column 2 starts at y=10
↓
code still demands y >= ~236
↓
it skips nearly the entire second column
↓
paragraph 2 becomes overset
```

I reproduced this against the current source.

Example:

```js
{
  width: 400,
  height: 260,
  padding: 10,
  bodyFontPx: 14,
  lineHeight: 1.25,
  columnCount: 2
}
```

with first paragraph approximately:

```js
'पहिला परिच्छेद मजकूर '.repeat(15)
```

and then:

```text
\n\n
दुसरा परिच्छेद नवीन स्तंभात सुरू होतो.
```

Current:

```text
paragraphSpacingPx = 0
→ paragraph 2 starts at top of column 2

paragraphSpacingPx = 8
→ paragraph 2 can disappear into overset
```

That is a real regression.

## Correct rule

Paragraph spacing is **local to a column**.

If paragraph 2 continues below paragraph 1 in the same column:

```text
apply paragraph spacing
```

If paragraph 1 exhausted the column and paragraph 2 moves to the next column:

```text
start at the normal top of the new column
```

Do NOT carry the previous column's absolute Y into the next column.

### Suggested implementation

Track which column owned the previous committed line.

For example:

```js
let lastLineColumnIndex = null;
```

When pushing a line:

```js
lastLineColumnIndex = colIndex;
```

At a forced paragraph break:

```js
if (
  paragraph.forcedBreak
  && lines.length
  && paragraphSpacingPx > 0
) {
  const previousColumn =
    lastLineColumnIndex;

  if (
    colIndex === previousColumn
  ) {
    // Apply paragraph spacing only inside this column.
    const targetY =
      lines[lines.length - 1].y
      + lines[lines.length - 1].height
      + paragraphSpacingPx;

    while (
      colIndex === previousColumn
    ) {
      if (
        !cursors[colIndex].hasRoom(bandHeight)
      ) {
        colIndex += 1;

        // NEW COLUMN:
        // spacing from old column no longer applies.
        break;
      }

      if (
        cursors[colIndex].y
        >= targetY - 0.5
      ) {
        break;
      }

      const row =
        cursors[colIndex].probe(
          bandHeight
        );

      if (!row) {
        colIndex += 1;
        break;
      }

      for (const gap of row.gaps) {
        emptyGapWidth +=
          gap.end - gap.start;
      }

      cursors[colIndex].commit(
        bandHeight
      );
    }
  }
}
```

Adapt to the cleanest current implementation.

The invariant is more important than exact code:

> **Paragraph vertical spacing must never propagate an absolute Y coordinate from one column into another.**

Add tests for:

* same-column paragraph spacing;
* paragraph ending at column bottom;
* next paragraph beginning at top of next column;
* same case where the previous paragraph's last line is a tall rich-size line.

```js
function naturalImageSize(url) {
  return new Promise(
    (resolve) => {
      const probe =
        new Image();

      probe.onload =
        () => {
          const width =
            Number(
              probe.naturalWidth
            );

          const height =
            Number(
              probe.naturalHeight
            );

          resolve(
            width > 0
            && height > 0
              ? {
                  width,
                  height,
                  ratio:
                    width /
                    height
                }
              : null
          );
        };

      probe.onerror =
        () => resolve(null);

      probe.src = url;
    }
  );
}
```

Then:

```js
const placement =
```

# 16. Normalize one image row

Suggested helper:

```js
export function imageInput(
  row
) {
  const frame = {
    x:
      Number(
        row.x_px ?? row.x
      ) || 0,

    y:
      Number(
        row.y_px ?? row.y
      ) || 0,

    width:
      Math.max(
        0,
        Number(
          row.width_px
          ?? row.width
        ) || 0
      ),

    height:
      Math.max(
        0,
        Number(
          row.height_px
          ?? row.height
        ) || 0
      )
  };

  const sourceWidth =
    Number(
      row.source_width_px
      ?? row.sourceWidth
    )
    || frame.width
    || 1;

  const sourceHeight =
    Number(
      row.source_height_px
      ?? row.sourceHeight
    )
    || frame.height
    || 1;

  return {
    frame,
    sourceWidth,
    sourceHeight,
    fitMode:
      normaliseFitMode(
        row.fit_mode
        ?? row.fitMode
      ),
    rotation:
      normaliseRotation(
        row.rotation
      ),
    flipH:
      Boolean(
        row.flip_h
        ?? row.flipH
      ),
    flipV:
      Boolean(
        row.flip_v
        ?? row.flipV
      ),
    crop: ...
  };
}
```

# 18. Fit geometry

For local unrotated target:

```text
target width = frame width
target height = frame height
```

For a quarter-turn:

```text
rotation 90/270
```

the local pre-rotation target axes are swapped.

Conceptually:

```js
const quarter =
  rotation % 180 !== 0;

const localTarget = {
  width:
    quarter
      ? frame.height
      : frame.width,

  height:
    quarter
      ? frame.width
      : frame.height
};
```

Resolve the source into this local target, then rotate the local result around the frame centre.

This preserves the current project's 90° rotation semantics without special CSS hacks in multiple places.

Given effective source crop:

```text
sw × sh
```

and local target:

```text
tw × th
```

```js
const scale =
  Math.min(
    tw / sw,
    th / sh
  );

const width =
  sw * scale;

const height =
  sh * scale;

const x =
  (tw - width) / 2;

const y =
  (th - height) / 2;
```

     ```js
     // Real Devanagari shaping. This is the exact authority font-metrics.js
     // claimed to be and was not.
     // [... extensive header documenting the measured overstatement table ...]
     
     const FONT_FILES = {
       'serif/400': '/assets/fonts/NotoSerifDevanagari-Regular.ttf',
       'serif/700': '/assets/fonts/NotoSerifDevanagari-Bold.ttf',
       'sans/400': '/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Regular.ttf',
       'sans/700': '/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Bold.ttf',
     };
     
     function faceKey(family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const stack = String(family).toLowerCase().includes('sans') ? 'sans' : 'serif';
       return `${stack}/${Number(weight) >= 600 ? 700 : 400}`;
     }
     
     async function readFontFile(path) { /* Node: fs read via import.meta.url-derived root; browser: fetch() */ }
     
     async function loadHarfBuzz() {
       if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions?.node) return import('harfbuzzjs');
       return import('/vendor/harfbuzz/index.mjs');
     }
     
     const fonts = new Map();
     let ready = null;
     
     export function ensureShaperReady() {
       if (ready) return ready;
       ready = (async () => {
         let hb;
         try { hb = await loadHarfBuzz(); } catch { return false; }
         await Promise.all(Object.entries(FONT_FILES).map(async ([key, path]) => {
           try {
             const bytes = await readFontFile(path);
             const blob = new hb.Blob(bytes);
             const face = new hb.Face(blob);
             const font = new hb.Font(face);
             font.setScale(face.upem, face.upem);
             fonts.set(key, { hb, face, font, upem: face.upem });
           } catch { /* missing face -> caller falls back for that weight/family */ }
         }));
         return fonts.size > 0;
       })();
       return ready;
     }
     
     export function isShaperReady() { return fonts.size > 0; }
     function shapedFace(family, weight) { return fonts.get(faceKey(family, weight)) || fonts.get('serif/400') || null; }
     
     const shapeCache = new Map();
     const CACHE_LIMIT = 20000;
     
     export function shapeWidthEm(text, family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const value = String(text || '');
       if (!value) return 0;
       const face = shapedFace(family, weight);
       if (!face) return null; // explicit null, never silently 0
       const key = `${faceKey(family, weight)} ${value}`;
       const hit = shapeCache.get(key);
       if (hit !== undefined) return hit;
       const buffer = new face.hb.Buffer();
       buffer.addText(value);
       buffer.guessSegmentProperties();
       face.hb.shape(face.font, buffer);
       const positions = buffer.getGlyphPositions();
       const em = positions.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.xAdvance, 0) / face.upem;
       if (shapeCache.size > CACHE_LIMIT) shapeCache.clear();
       shapeCache.set(key, em);
       return em;
     }
     
     export function shapeWidthPx(text, fontPx, family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const em = shapeWidthEm(text, family, weight);
       return em === null ? null : em * (Number(fontPx) || 0);
     }
     
     export function shapeRun(text, { family = 'serif', weight = 400, fontPx = 16 } = {}) {
       const face = shapedFace(family, weight);
       if (!face) return null;
       const buffer = new face.hb.Buffer();
       buffer.addText(String(text || ''));
       buffer.guessSegmentProperties();
       face.hb.shape(face.font, buffer);
       const infos = buffer.getGlyphInfos();
       const positions = buffer.getGlyphPositions();
       const scale = fontPx / face.upem;
       let width = 0;
       const glyphs = infos.map((info, i) => {
         const pos = positions[i];
         const glyph = { glyphId: info.codepoint, cluster: info.cluster,
           xAdvance: pos.xAdvance*scale, xOffset: pos.xOffset*scale, yOffset: pos.yOffset*scale, x: width+pos.xOffset*scale };
         width += pos.xAdvance * scale;
         return glyph;
       });
       return { width, glyphs, ready: true };
     }
     ```

```js
export function publicationFamily(value = "") {
  const v = String(value).toLowerCase();
  if (
    v.includes("sans") ||
    v.includes("arial") ||
    v.includes("helvetica")
  ) {
    return {
      key: "sans",
      css: "'Noto Sans Devanagari', sans-serif",
    };
  }

  return {
    key: "serif",
    css: "'Noto Serif Devanagari', serif",
  };
}
```

```js
function styleForRange(marks, start, end, base) {
  const active = marks.filter(
    m => m.end > start && m.start < end
  );

  return {
    family: base.family,
    weight:
      active.some(m => m.tag === "b")

        : base.weight,
    italic: active.some(m => m.tag === "i"),
    underline: active.some(m => m.tag === "u"),
    fontPx:

      ?? base.fontPx,
    letterSpacingPx: base.letterSpacingPx,
  };
}
```

```js
function beginSemanticTextEdit(part) {
  const isHeadline = part === "headline";

  const source = isHeadline
    ? state.view.headline
    : state.view.subheading;

  const band = isHeadline
    ? composition?.bands?.headline
    : composition?.bands?.deck;

  const overlay = document.createElement("div");
  overlay.contentEditable = "plaintext-only";
  overlay.className = "frame-semantic-text-editor";
  overlay.textContent = source;

  overlay.style.left = `${band.left ?? 0}px`;
  overlay.style.top = `${band.top}px`;
  overlay.style.width = `${band.width ?? state.view.width}px`;
  overlay.style.minHeight = `${Math.max(24, band.height)}px`;

  // Commit FULL overlay.textContent through existing patch path.
}
```

```js
function activateBodyEditor() {
  hooks.onSelectPart?.("body");

  const writing = document.getElementById("edWritingSurface");
  writing?.classList.add("is-body-target");
  writing?.scrollIntoView({
    behavior: "smooth",
    block: "nearest"
  });

  requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    if (!quill) return;
    quill.focus();

    const selection = quill.getSelection();
    if (!selection) {
      const length = Math.max(0, quill.getLength() - 1);
      quill.setSelection(length, 0, "silent");
    }
  });
}
```

# 2. `sourcePointToFrame()`

Required transform order must match paint:

```text
source pixels
→ crop-relative coordinates
→ fitted content rectangle
→ flip H/V
→ quarter-turn rotation
→ frame coordinates
```

Conceptually:

```js
export function sourcePointToFrame(
  resolved,
  sourceX,
  sourceY
) {
  const {
    frame,
    crop,
    localTarget,
    localContentRect,
    flipH,
    flipV,
    rotation
  } = resolved;

  let u =
    (
      sourceX -
      crop.x
    ) /
    crop.width;

  let v =
    (
      sourceY -
      crop.y
    ) /
    crop.height;

  if (flipH) {
    u = 1 - u;
  }

  if (flipV) {
    v = 1 - v;
  }

  let x =
    localContentRect.x +
    u *
    localContentRect.width;

  let y =
    localContentRect.y +
    v *
    localContentRect.height;

  const cx =
    localTarget.width / 2;

  const cy =
    localTarget.height / 2;

  const dx = x - cx;
  const dy = y - cy;

  switch (
    ((rotation % 360) + 360) % 360
  ) {
    case 0:
      break;

    case 90:
      [x, y] = [
        cx - dy,
        cy + dx
      ];
      break;

    case 180:
      [x, y] = [
        cx - dx,
        cy - dy
      ];
      break;

    case 270:
      [x, y] = [
        cx + dy,
        cy - dx
      ];
      break;

    default:
      // Do not silently claim exactness.
      return null;
  }

  return {
    x:
      frame.x +
      frame.width / 2 -
      localTarget.width / 2 +
      x,

    y:
      frame.y +
      frame.height / 2 -
      localTarget.height / 2 +
      y
  };
}
```

This pseudocode is a guide.

**Verify signs/centres against the browser paint.**

Do not blindly copy it if current `localTarget` quarter-turn semantics require a different centre conversion.

```text
intersect rect with source crop
if empty → null

map four corners through sourcePointToFrame()

bounds =
min/max transformed X/Y

clip against placement frame
return bounds
```

For 0/90/180/270 this gives exact axis-aligned transformed mask-cell bounds.

For arbitrary persisted rotation that is not a quarter-turn:

```text
do NOT use stale alpha mask
```

Use conservative full-frame exclusion.

The Editor creates quarter turns only, so quarter turns are the required exact path.

# 7. FIX `placementsByEdition()`

Join `media_assets`.

Return every composition-affecting field:

```sql
SELECT
  si.page_section_id,

  si.x_px,
  si.y_px,
  si.width_px,
  si.height_px,

  si.crop_x_px,
  si.crop_y_px,
  si.crop_width_px,
  si.crop_height_px,

  si.rotation,
  si.flip_h,
  si.flip_v,

  si.shape,
  si.stand_off_px,
  si.mask,
  si.fit_mode,

  ma.width_px
    AS source_width_px,

  ma.height_px
    AS source_height_px

FROM section_images si

JOIN media_assets ma
  ON ma.id =
     si.media_asset_id

JOIN page_sections s
  ON s.id =
     si.page_section_id

JOIN pages p
  ON p.id =
     s.page_id

WHERE p.newspaper_id = $1
```

Preserve ordering.

# 1. FIRST: ONE REAL REMAINING #9 BUG FOUND BY SOURCE AUDIT

Do this before Smart Cards.

The quarter-turn cutout transform itself is now implemented correctly through:

```text
image-geometry.js
→ sourceRectToFrameBounds()
→ exclusion.js
```

However `obstacleIntervals()` still performs an **incorrect early vertical rejection** before reaching that exact cutout path.

Current logic begins approximately:

```js
const pad = standOffPx(
  image,
  bodyFontPx
);

const box =
  boxOf(
    image,
    pad
  );

if (
  bottom <= box.top ||
  top >= box.bottom
) {
  return [];
}
```

`boxOf()` rotates the stored placement rectangle.

That does NOT match how quarter-turn painting now works.

The stored placement frame itself remains fixed.

For a 90°/270° image, `picture-style.js` first swaps the inner image's local target axes and then rotates that inner image around the fixed frame centre.

Therefore a 100×200 placement rotated 90° still visually occupies the **100×200 placement frame**.

But `boxOf()` currently treats the 100×200 frame as though the frame itself rotated and produces roughly a 200×100 vertical gate.

That can reject valid cutout occupancy before the exact transformed mask is even evaluated.

   - **The scanline/interval CompositionResult architecture** (frozen, must be kept): `PAGE GEOMETRY → FRAME GEOMETRY → ORDERED EDITORIAL FLOWS → HORIZONTAL LINE BANDS → COLUMN INTERVALS minus IMAGE EXCLUSION INTERVALS → SHAPED TEXT RUNS → one CompositionResult`. Implemented across `font-metrics.js`, `graphemes.js`, `intervals.js`, `exclusion.js`, `compose.js`, `render.js`, `section-adapter.js`.
   - **Real Devanagari shaping (GSUB/GPOS) vs raw hmtx-advance-summing**: the critical, now-triply-confirmed defect. Devanagari conjuncts (क्ष, ज्ञान, श्री, कर्म, ज्ञानेश्वर) collapse to fewer, narrower ligature glyphs via GSUB; summing per-codepoint hmtx advances overstates their width by 26–81% depending on the specific conjunct. Fixed via a real HarfBuzz WASM shaper (`harfbuzzjs` npm package, MIT-ish/OFL-adjacent license, v1.6.0).
   - **harfbuzzjs API** (verified via direct testing): pure ESM (`type:module`), top-level-await self-initializing (`init(await createHarfBuzz())` inside `index.mjs`, meaning `import`/`await import()` alone is sufficient, no separate manual init call needed). Core classes: `Blob`, `Face` (has `.upem`), `Font` (has `.setScale(x,y)`), `Buffer` (has `.addText()`, `.guessSegmentProperties()` — this is the CORRECT idiomatic call, NOT manual `setScript`/`setLanguage`/`setDirection`, which I found produces broken zero-width results if `guessSegmentProperties()` is skipped), `.getGlyphInfos()`, `.getGlyphPositions()` (each position has `xAdvance`,`yAdvance`,`xOffset`,`yOffset` in the font's set scale). Top-level function `hb.shape(font, buffer)`.
   - **Dual Node/browser module loading pattern** (already established by font-metrics.js, now replicated in shaper.js): Node reaches the real package via `import('harfbuzzjs')`/`node:fs/promises` reading from `public/assets/fonts/`; browser fetches from a vendored, statically-served copy — new addition: `public/vendor/harfbuzz/` (containing `index.mjs`, `harfbuzz.js`, `harfbuzz.wasm`, `index.d.mts`, `LICENSE`), imported via `import('/vendor/harfbuzz/index.mjs')`. Confirmed via `server.js:45` (`app.use(express.static(path.join(__dirname,"public")))`) that this will be correctly served. Confirmed via inspecting `harfbuzz.js`'s emscripten glue that `.wasm` location is derived relative to `import.meta.url`, so directory-relative vendoring works in both runtimes without extra configuration.
   - **UAX #29 grapheme clusters** (`Intl.Segmenter('mr',{granularity:'grapheme'})`, existing, correct, unchanged) — text is only ever measured/cut at akshara boundaries via `graphemes.js`'s `clusters()`/`breakPieces()`/`trimEndClusters()`/`clusterCount()`.
   - **Forced vs optional line breaks**: `graphemes.js`'s `BREAK_AFTER = /[\s।॥\-–—/]/` currently treats `\n` (which matches `\s`) as an ORDINARY optional break — confirmed bug, needs a paragraph-aware preprocessing layer (planned to live in `compose.js`, not `graphemes.js`) that distinguishes single `\n` (line/list forced break) from `\n\n` (paragraph forced break, normally also gets extra visual spacing — deferred in this pass per an explicit, documented scope decision).
   - **Rich text infrastructure** (`public/editor/layout/rich-text.js`, existing, correct, being built ON rather than replaced): `plainText()`, `textWithMarks()` (returns `{text, marks:[{start,end,tag}]}`, tag ∈ {b,i,u}), `markRun()`, `sanitise()`, `fromPlainText()`. Critically: `plainText()` and `textWithMarks()` produce IDENTICAL underlying `text` for the same HTML input (same tag/newline/entity normalization pipeline), which is WHY `render.js`'s currently-separate re-derivation of marks via character offsets happens to already be positionally correct today, even though the WIDTH used for line-breaking upstream ignores marks entirely (the actual bug).
   - **CSS ground truth for typography** (`public/styles.css`, read directly, decisive): `.section-headline, .section-kicker, .section-subheading { font-family: "Sahas Sans", ... }` (sans, weight 700 for headline/kicker, 400 for subheading/deck); `.newspaper-canvas { font-family: "Sahas Serif", ... }` (body inherits serif, weight 400); `.section-body { text-align: justify; ... }` — this rule is now DEAD for the new engine because composed lines render as `.section-composed`/`.section-body-line` absolutely-positioned spans, never inside a `.section-body` container, so the persisted `text_align`/`textAlign` field (real, already fully wired end-to-end: `typography-panel.js`'s `ALIGNMENTS=[left,center,right,justify]`, `section-model.js` default `"left"`, `pageSection.service.js`, `page.repository.js`'s `text_align = COALESCE($29,...)`) is currently silently ignored by the new compose.js.
   - **`FONT_FAMILIES` UI list** (`typography-panel.js`): `["", "Georgia...", "Times New Roman...", "Noto Serif Devanagari...", "Arial...", "Helvetica Neue..."]`, default `""` ("Theme default") — an existing body-only family-override control, distinct from the headline/kicker/deck sans-vs-serif split; I was mid-decision on how this should interact with new per-flow typography defaults when the summary was requested.
   - **Test count integrity discipline** (learned earlier this session via a real self-caused bug, now explicitly codified in the master brief's Section 1 safety rules): never overwrite an existing test file with `Write`; always check/merge; a suite "staying green" after a change is not proof nothing was lost — compare actual test counts.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`public/editor/compose/shaper.js`** (NEW FILE, fully written and committed to disk in this phase, NOT yet git-committed) — the HarfBuzz-backed exact shaping module. Full content as written:
     ```js
     // Real Devanagari shaping. This is the exact authority font-metrics.js
     // claimed to be and was not.
     // [... extensive header documenting the measured overstatement table ...]
     
     const FONT_FILES = {
       'serif/400': '/assets/fonts/NotoSerifDevanagari-Regular.ttf',
       'serif/700': '/assets/fonts/NotoSerifDevanagari-Bold.ttf',
       'sans/400': '/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Regular.ttf',
       'sans/700': '/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Bold.ttf',
     };
     
     function faceKey(family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const stack = String(family).toLowerCase().includes('sans') ? 'sans' : 'serif';
       return `${stack}/${Number(weight) >= 600 ? 700 : 400}`;
     }
     
     async function readFontFile(path) { /* Node: fs read via import.meta.url-derived root; browser: fetch() */ }
     
     async function loadHarfBuzz() {
       if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions?.node) return import('harfbuzzjs');
       return import('/vendor/harfbuzz/index.mjs');
     }
     
     const fonts = new Map();
     let ready = null;
     
     export function ensureShaperReady() {
       if (ready) return ready;
       ready = (async () => {
         let hb;
         try { hb = await loadHarfBuzz(); } catch { return false; }
         await Promise.all(Object.entries(FONT_FILES).map(async ([key, path]) => {
           try {
             const bytes = await readFontFile(path);
             const blob = new hb.Blob(bytes);
             const face = new hb.Face(blob);
             const font = new hb.Font(face);
             font.setScale(face.upem, face.upem);
             fonts.set(key, { hb, face, font, upem: face.upem });
           } catch { /* missing face -> caller falls back for that weight/family */ }
         }));
         return fonts.size > 0;
       })();
       return ready;
     }
     
     export function isShaperReady() { return fonts.size > 0; }
     function shapedFace(family, weight) { return fonts.get(faceKey(family, weight)) || fonts.get('serif/400') || null; }
     
     const shapeCache = new Map();
     const CACHE_LIMIT = 20000;
     
     export function shapeWidthEm(text, family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const value = String(text || '');
       if (!value) return 0;
       const face = shapedFace(family, weight);
       if (!face) return null; // explicit null, never silently 0
       const key = `${faceKey(family, weight)} ${value}`;
       const hit = shapeCache.get(key);
       if (hit !== undefined) return hit;
       const buffer = new face.hb.Buffer();
       buffer.addText(value);
       buffer.guessSegmentProperties();
       face.hb.shape(face.font, buffer);
       const positions = buffer.getGlyphPositions();
       const em = positions.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.xAdvance, 0) / face.upem;
       if (shapeCache.size > CACHE_LIMIT) shapeCache.clear();
       shapeCache.set(key, em);
       return em;
     }
     
     export function shapeWidthPx(text, fontPx, family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const em = shapeWidthEm(text, family, weight);
       return em === null ? null : em * (Number(fontPx) || 0);
     }
     
     export function shapeRun(text, { family = 'serif', weight = 400, fontPx = 16 } = {}) {
       const face = shapedFace(family, weight);
       if (!face) return null;
       const buffer = new face.hb.Buffer();
       buffer.addText(String(text || ''));
       buffer.guessSegmentProperties();
       face.hb.shape(face.font, buffer);
       const infos = buffer.getGlyphInfos();
       const positions = buffer.getGlyphPositions();
       const scale = fontPx / face.upem;
       let width = 0;
       const glyphs = infos.map((info, i) => {
         const pos = positions[i];
         const glyph = { glyphId: info.codepoint, cluster: info.cluster,
           xAdvance: pos.xAdvance*scale, xOffset: pos.xOffset*scale, yOffset: pos.yOffset*scale, x: width+pos.xOffset*scale };
         width += pos.xAdvance * scale;
         return glyph;
       });
       return { width, glyphs, ready: true };
     }
     ```
     Verified working end-to-end via a direct smoke test (`node ./shapertest.mjs` from project root): `ensureShaperReady()`→true, and produced exactly the expected shaped widths matching the earlier raw-HarfBuzz verification (क्ष=0.6950em/11.12px@16, ज्ञान=1.35em, श्री=0.885em, कर्म=1.267em, शेतकऱ्यांसाठी=4.644em, ज्ञानेश्वर=2.41em; sans/700 `विज्ञान`=2.523em; `shapeRun('क्ष',{fontPx:32})` → width 22.24, exactly 1 glyph).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **First harfbuzzjs shaping attempt produced all-zero widths**: my first smoke-test script explicitly called `buffer.setScript('Deva'); buffer.setLanguage('mr'); buffer.setDirection('ltr');` without calling `buffer.guessSegmentProperties()`. Result: `xAdvance: 0` for every glyph, and glyph-count exactly equal to codepoint-count (no real GSUB substitution happening at all) — e.g. `क् ष` (3 codepoints) → 3 glyphs, 0 width. Fixed by switching to the idiomatic `buffer.guessSegmentProperties()` call (dropping the manual script/language/direction calls entirely), which immediately produced correct results (क → xAdvance 711, matching the already-known hmtx value exactly, and क्ष → 1 glyph with real width). Root cause not fully diagnosed (likely a buffer-properties ordering/interaction requirement specific to harfbuzzjs's binding), but the fix is confirmed correct and is now the pattern used in the final `shaper.js`.
   - **Scratchpad-relative script failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `harfbuzzjs`**: running `node /tmp/.../scratchpad/hbtest.mjs` failed because bare-specifier `import 'harfbuzzjs'` resolution requires being inside (or below) a directory containing the relevant `node_modules`. export function publicationFamily(value = "") {
```js
  const v = String(value).toLowerCase();
  if (
    v.includes("sans") ||
    v.includes("arial") ||
    v.includes("helvetica")
  ) {
    return {
      key: "sans",
      css: "'Noto Sans Devanagari', sans-serif",
    };
  }

  return {
    key: "serif",
    css: "'Noto Serif Devanagari', serif",
  };
}
```

# 4. FIRST TASK — FIX THE CURRENT LINE-HEIGHT DESIGN MISTAKE

Do this **before Phase C masthead work**.

The latest commit `1ea030d` fixed inline-size overlap by finding the largest inline font anywhere in the entire body and using that height for the whole body's band grid.

That prevents overlap but damages fill.

Example:

```text
base body = 16px

one selected word = 40px
```

Current behavior can make **every line** roughly 40px-sized even though only one line contains the large word.

That can turn a previously fitting article into overset and create excessive whitespace.

This violates the main goal of accurate fill.

## Required result

Only the line that actually contains the larger run should get the larger line box.

Example:

```text
normal line → normal height
normal line → normal height
40px word line → larger height
normal line → normal height
normal line → normal height
```

Do not use one maximum font size for the entire flow.

---

# 5. Implement variable per-line body height

Primary file:

```text
public/editor/compose/compose.js
```

The algorithm must remain deterministic and bounded.

For each line:

```text
1. Start from base body line height.
2. Query legal intervals for that provisional vertical band.
3. Fit candidate text/runs into the interval.
4. Determine the maximum actual line-box requirement of runs ON THAT LINE.
5. If required height differs materially:
      query obstacles again using the larger vertical band
      and refit this line once.
6. Finalize the line.
7. Next Y = this finalized line's real bottom.
```

Maximum two passes per line.

Pseudo:

```js
function composeBodyLineAt({
  y,
  column,
  remaining,
  baseStyle,
  ...
}) {
  const baseHeight =
    baseStyle.fontPx *
    baseStyle.lineHeight;

  let bandHeight = baseHeight;
  let result = null;

  for (let pass = 0; pass < 2; pass += 1) {
    const intervals = viableIntervalsForBand(
      column,
      y,
      y + bandHeight,
      images,
      ...
    );

    result = fitBodyLine(
      intervals,
      remaining,
      ...
    );

    if (!result) break;

    const requiredHeight = Math.max(
      baseHeight,
      ...result.runs.map((run) =>
        run.fontPx *
        minLineHeightFor(
          run.family,
          run.weight
        )
      )
    );

    if (
      Math.abs(requiredHeight - bandHeight)
      < 0.25
    ) {
      break;
    }

    bandHeight = requiredHeight;
  }

  if (!result) return null;

  return {
    ...result,
    y,
    height: bandHeight,
    bottom: y + bandHeight
  };
}
```

Adapt to current interval/pour implementation instead of blindly copying names.

The critical invariant is:

```text
line height depends only on the runs actually placed on that line
```

Image obstacle sampling must use the whole final vertical line band.

# 12. Repository structural repair

File:

```text
src/repositories/page.repository.js
```

Add an idempotent helper approximately:

```js
async function ensureStructuralTemplateFrames(
  pageId,
  { tx } = {}
) {
  const db = tx || pool;

  const page =
    await findPageMeta(pageId, db);

  if (!page) return null;

  const template =
    resolveTemplateForPage(page);

  const stored =
    await listSectionKeys(pageId, db);

  const existing =
    new Set(stored);

  const created = [];

  for (const section of template.sections) {
    if (
      !isStructuralTemplateFrame(section)
    ) {
      continue;
    }

    if (existing.has(section.key)) {
      continue;
    }

    await insertTemplateSection(
      pageId,
      section,
      db
    );

    created.push(section.key);
  }

  return { created };
}
```

Reuse existing repository SQL/helpers rather than creating duplicate insertion logic.


# 26. Resize geometry

Pure helper:

```js
resizeRect(
  rect,
  handle,
  dx,
  dy,
  {
    bounds,
    minWidth,
    minHeight,
    preserveAspect
  }
)
```

Base:

```js
if (handle.includes("e")) {
  width += dx;
}

if (handle.includes("s")) {
  height += dy;
}

if (handle.includes("w")) {
  x += dx;
  width -= dx;
}
```

# BUG 1 — LARGE INLINE RUN NEAR THE BOTTOM CAN STILL REPORT `FITS` WHILE PAINTING OUTSIDE THE FRAME

Current `fillRow()` approximately does:

```js
if (
  Math.abs(requiredHeight - height) < 0.25
  || pass === 1
  || !cursor.hasRoom(requiredHeight)
) {
  break;
}
```

The `!cursor.hasRoom(requiredHeight)` branch is wrong.

Current behavior:

```text
base body line fits vertically
↓
line contains a 40px selected word
↓
actual required line height is ~62px
↓
62px does NOT fit before frame bottom
↓
fillRow keeps the first base-height attempt
↓
cursor commits ~25px
↓
40px word can visually extend beyond the frame
↓
fitState can still be FITS
↓
no overset/violation
```

I reproduced this against the current uploaded source.

A configuration around:

```js
{
  width: 180,
  height: 95,
  padding: 10,
  bodyFontPx: 16,
  lineHeight: 1.25,
  columnCount: 1
}
```

with a final `data-sahas-size=40` token can currently produce approximately:

```text
fitState: FITS
line.height: ~24.88
actual 40px run requirement: ~62.2
violations: []
```

This is unacceptable.

## Correct behavior

If the candidate row needs more height than the current column has:

**do not consume the text**
**do not commit the short row**
**do not paint it with an undersized line box**

Instead:

```text
retry the SAME unconsumed text in the next column
```

If there is no later column with enough room:

```text
leave that copy in overset
```

or emit an explicit hard violation.

The composition must never say FITS while a run requires more vertical space than its line owns.

### Suggested implementation

Let `fillRow()` return a retry signal:

```js
if (
  requiredHeight > height + 0.25
  && !cursor.hasRoom(requiredHeight)
) {
  return {
    retryNextColumn: true
  };
}
```

Caller:

```js
const result = fillRow(...);

if (result?.retryNextColumn) {
  colIndex += 1;
  continue;
}
```

Important:

* `index` must remain unchanged.
* `paraCharOffset` must remain unchanged.
* current cursor must NOT commit.
* current text must be retried at the top/current position of the next column.
* if no column can accept it, normal trailing overset accounting must capture it.

Do not silently keep the undersized first pass.

### Required invariant

For every placed line:

```js
line.y + line.height <= content.bottom + tolerance
```

and:

```js
line.height >= requiredHeightOfEveryRunOnThatLine
```

Add tests.

# BUG 2 — PARAGRAPH SPACING IS CARRIED ACROSS COLUMNS USING THE OLD COLUMN'S ABSOLUTE Y

Current forced-paragraph code approximately computes:

```js
const nextY =
  lastLine.y
  + lastLine.height
  + paragraphSpacingPx;
```

and then advances the current cursor until:

```js
cursor.y >= nextY
```

That is correct only when the next paragraph continues in the **same column**.

It is wrong when the previous paragraph ends at the bottom of column 1 and the new paragraph must start in column 2.

Current behavior can become:

```text
paragraph 1 ends near y=228 in column 1
paragraphSpacingPx = 8
↓
column 1 has no room
↓
move to column 2
↓
column 2 starts at y=10
↓
code still demands y >= ~236
↓
it skips nearly the entire second column
↓
paragraph 2 becomes overset
```

I reproduced this against the current source.

Example:

```js
{
  width: 400,
  height: 260,
  padding: 10,
  bodyFontPx: 14,
  lineHeight: 1.25,
  columnCount: 2
}
```

with first paragraph approximately:

```js
'पहिला परिच्छेद मजकूर '.repeat(15)
```

and then:

```text
\n\n
दुसरा परिच्छेद नवीन स्तंभात सुरू होतो.
```

Current:

```text
paragraphSpacingPx = 0
→ paragraph 2 starts at top of column 2

paragraphSpacingPx = 8
→ paragraph 2 can disappear into overset
```

That is a real regression.

## Correct rule

Paragraph spacing is **local to a column**.

If paragraph 2 continues below paragraph 1 in the same column:

```text
apply paragraph spacing
```

If paragraph 1 exhausted the column and paragraph 2 moves to the next column:

```text
start at the normal top of the new column
```

Do NOT carry the previous column's absolute Y into the next column.

### Suggested implementation

Track which column owned the previous committed line.

For example:

```js
let lastLineColumnIndex = null;
```

When pushing a line:

```js
lastLineColumnIndex = colIndex;
```

At a forced paragraph break:

```js
if (
  paragraph.forcedBreak
  && lines.length
  && paragraphSpacingPx > 0
) {
  const previousColumn =
    lastLineColumnIndex;

  if (
    colIndex === previousColumn
  ) {
    // Apply paragraph spacing only inside this column.
    const targetY =
      lines[lines.length - 1].y
      + lines[lines.length - 1].height
      + paragraphSpacingPx;

    while (
      colIndex === previousColumn
    ) {
      if (
        !cursors[colIndex].hasRoom(bandHeight)
      ) {
        colIndex += 1;

        // NEW COLUMN:
        // spacing from old column no longer applies.
        break;
      }

      if (
        cursors[colIndex].y
        >= targetY - 0.5
      ) {
        break;
      }

      const row =
        cursors[colIndex].probe(
          bandHeight
        );

      if (!row) {
        colIndex += 1;
        break;
      }

      for (const gap of row.gaps) {
        emptyGapWidth +=
          gap.end - gap.start;
      }

      cursors[colIndex].commit(
        bandHeight
      );
    }
  }
}
```

Adapt to the cleanest current implementation.

The invariant is more important than exact code:

> **Paragraph vertical spacing must never propagate an absolute Y coordinate from one column into another.**

Add tests for:

* same-column paragraph spacing;
* paragraph ending at column bottom;
* next paragraph beginning at top of next column;
* same case where the previous paragraph's last line is a tall rich-size line.

```js

```

with something like:

```js
function naturalImageSize(url) {
  return new Promise(
    (resolve) => {
      const probe =
        new Image();

      probe.onload =
        () => {
          const width =
            Number(
              probe.naturalWidth
            );

          const height =
            Number(
              probe.naturalHeight
            );

          resolve(
            width > 0
            && height > 0
              ? {
                  width,
                  height,
                  ratio:
                    width /
                    height
                }
              : null
          );
        };

      probe.onerror =
        () => resolve(null);

      probe.src = url;
    }
  );
}
```

Then:

```js
const source =
  await naturalImageSize(url);

const placement =
  source
    ? placeInside(
        section,
        source.ratio
      )
    : null;

```

# 16. Normalize one image row

Suggested helper:

```js
export function imageInput(
  row
) {
  const frame = {
    x:
      Number(
        row.x_px ?? row.x
      ) || 0,

    y:
      Number(
        row.y_px ?? row.y
      ) || 0,

    width:
      Math.max(
        0,
        Number(
          row.width_px
          ?? row.width
        ) || 0
      ),

    height:
      Math.max(
        0,
        Number(
          row.height_px
          ?? row.height
        ) || 0
      )
  };

  const sourceWidth =
    Number(
      row.source_width_px
      ?? row.sourceWidth
    )
    || frame.width
    || 1;

  const sourceHeight =
    Number(
      row.source_height_px
      ?? row.sourceHeight
    )
    || frame.height
    || 1;

  return {
    frame,
    sourceWidth,
    sourceHeight,
    fitMode:
      normaliseFitMode(
        row.fit_mode
        ?? row.fitMode
      ),
    rotation:
      normaliseRotation(
        row.rotation
      ),
    flipH:
      Boolean(
        row.flip_h
        ?? row.flipH
      ),
    flipV:
      Boolean(
        row.flip_v
        ?? row.flipV
      ),
    crop: ...
  };
}
```

# 18. Fit geometry

For local unrotated target:

```text
target width = frame width
target height = frame height
```

For a quarter-turn:

```text
rotation 90/270
```

the local pre-rotation target axes are swapped.

Conceptually:

```js
const quarter =
  rotation % 180 !== 0;

const localTarget = {
  width:
    quarter
      ? frame.height
      : frame.width,

  height:
    quarter
      ? frame.width
      : frame.height
};
```

Resolve the source into this local target, then rotate the local result around the frame centre.

This preserves the current project's 90° rotation semantics without special CSS hacks in multiple places.

---

# 19. Contain

Given effective source crop:

```text
sw × sh
```

and local target:

```text
tw × th
```

```js
const scale =
  Math.min(
    tw / sw,
    th / sh
  );

const width =
  sw * scale;

const height =
  sh * scale;

const x =
  (tw - width) / 2;

const y =
  (th - height) / 2;
```

---

# 20. Cover

```js
const scale =
  Math.max(
    tw / sw,
    th / sh
  );
```

Source fills target.

Anything outside target is clipped.

This intentionally distorts the source.

This is required.

Do not preserve ratio in Stretch.

# 25. Paint semantics

### Contain

Show the whole cropped source.

No cropping.

Blank area inside the placement frame is allowed.

### Cover

Fill the entire placement frame.

Clip excess.

Frame must:

```css
overflow:hidden
```

### Stretch

Fill both frame axes independently.

No aspect lock.

### Ellipse

Ellipse clipping applies at the frame.

### Cutout

Transparent pixels remain transparent.

The visible cutout subject is transformed by the same source/content geometry.

   - **`boxOf()`'s corrected quarter-turn handling** (`exclusion.js`): a quarter turn (0/90/180/270) never grows the picture's outer footprint since the frame itself is fixed and only content rotates within it — `boxOf()` now returns the frame's own unrotated box for any multiple of 90°, and only applies cos/sin-widening for genuinely in-between angles (which the Editor's Rotate control cannot even produce).
   - **Smart Cards architecture** (`public/editor/smart-cards/`): `smart_card_key`/`smart_card_data` (JSONB) hold what's IN a block; `feature_key` holds what the layout RESERVED it for (read-only). `smartCardText()` renders data to body copy for measurement purposes only (character grid, worklist, preflight, fit action) — never the source of truth. New: `layoutSmartCard()` is a pure geometry solver (no DOM), same pattern as `compose/` and `image-geometry.js` — same input always gives same output in Node and browser.
   - **Bounded font-size solver pattern**: `CANDIDATE_FONT_PX = [9, 8, 7.5, 7, 6.5, 6, 5.5]`, tried largest-first, first fit wins, never infinite loop — shared by rashi/panchang/suvichar/dinvishesh via `solveFont(availableHeight, neededHeight)`.
   - **Clamp-not-shrink pattern for OVERSET**: geometry solvers clamp to a documented minimum legible size (`MIN_SUDOKU_CELL_PX=10`, `MIN_CARD_FONT_PX=5.5`) rather than silently shrinking past it — the card still draws at a legible size, just flagged, never deleted.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **SAHAS architecture invariants** (from CLAUDE.md, still governing): Route→Controller→Service→Repository→PostgreSQL; AI never owns data; px vs mm never mixed silently; the composition engine lives in `public/editor/compose/`; "no bundler — `<script type="module">` + dynamic `import()`"; third-party browser libs are vendored under `public/vendor/<name>/` (established precedent: `public/vendor/quill/`); dev server restart discipline (kill by port via `ss -ltnpH`, never `pkill -f`, relaunch via `setsid nohup node server.js &`); disposable-edition discipline (`2099-*` dates only for any DB mutation/testing).
   - **The scanline/interval CompositionResult architecture** (frozen, must be kept): `PAGE GEOMETRY → FRAME GEOMETRY → ORDERED EDITORIAL FLOWS → HORIZONTAL LINE BANDS → COLUMN INTERVALS minus IMAGE EXCLUSION INTERVALS → SHAPED TEXT RUNS → one CompositionResult`. Implemented across `font-metrics.js`, `graphemes.js`, `intervals.js`, `exclusion.js`, `compose.js`, `render.js`, `section-adapter.js`.
   - **Real Devanagari shaping (GSUB/GPOS) vs raw hmtx-advance-summing**: the critical, now-triply-confirmed defect. Devanagari conjuncts (क्ष, ज्ञान, श्री, कर्म, ज्ञानेश्वर) collapse to fewer, narrower ligature glyphs via GSUB; summing per-codepoint hmtx advances overstates their width by 26–81% depending on the specific conjunct. Fixed via a real HarfBuzz WASM shaper (`harfbuzzjs` npm package, MIT-ish/OFL-adjacent license, v1.6.0).
   - **harfbuzzjs API** (verified via direct testing): pure ESM (`type:module`), top-level-await self-initializing (`init(await createHarfBuzz())` inside `index.mjs`, meaning `import`/`await import()` alone is sufficient, no separate manual init call needed). Core classes: `Blob`, `Face` (has `.upem`), `Font` (has `.setScale(x,y)`), `Buffer` (has `.addText()`, `.guessSegmentProperties()` — this is the CORRECT idiomatic call, NOT manual `setScript`/`setLanguage`/`setDirection`, which I found produces broken zero-width results if `guessSegmentProperties()` is skipped), `.getGlyphInfos()`, `.getGlyphPositions()` (each position has `xAdvance`,`yAdvance`,`xOffset`,`yOffset` in the font's set scale). Top-level function `hb.shape(font, buffer)`.
   - **Dual Node/browser module loading pattern** (already established by font-metrics.js, now replicated in shaper.js): Node reaches the real package via `import('harfbuzzjs')`/`node:fs/promises` reading from `public/assets/fonts/`; browser fetches from a vendored, statically-served copy — new addition: `public/vendor/harfbuzz/` (containing `index.mjs`, `harfbuzz.js`, `harfbuzz.wasm`, `index.d.mts`, `LICENSE`), imported via `import('/vendor/harfbuzz/index.mjs')`. Confirmed via `server.js:45` (`app.use(express.static(path.join(__dirname,"public")))`) that this will be correctly served. Confirmed via inspecting `harfbuzz.js`'s emscripten glue that `.wasm` location is derived relative to `import.meta.url`, so directory-relative vendoring works in both runtimes without extra configuration.
   - **UAX #29 grapheme clusters** (`Intl.Segmenter('mr',{granularity:'grapheme'})`, existing, correct, unchanged) — text is only ever measured/cut at akshara boundaries via `graphemes.js`'s `clusters()`/`breakPieces()`/`trimEndClusters()`/`clusterCount()`.
   - **Forced vs optional line breaks**: `graphemes.js`'s `BREAK_AFTER = /[\s।॥\-–—/]/` currently treats `\n` (which matches `\s`) as an ORDINARY optional break — confirmed bug, needs a paragraph-aware preprocessing layer (planned to live in `compose.js`, not `graphemes.js`) that distinguishes single `\n` (line/list forced break) from `\n\n` (paragraph forced break, normally also gets extra visual spacing — deferred in this pass per an explicit, documented scope decision).
   - **Rich text infrastructure** (`public/editor/layout/rich-text.js`, existing, correct, being built ON rather than replaced): `plainText()`, `textWithMarks()` (returns `{text, marks:[{start,end,tag}]}`, tag ∈ {b,i,u}), `markRun()`, `sanitise()`, `fromPlainText()`. Critically: `plainText()` and `textWithMarks()` produce IDENTICAL underlying `text` for the same HTML input (same tag/newline/entity normalization pipeline), which is WHY `render.js`'s currently-separate re-derivation of marks via character offsets happens to already be positionally correct today, even though the WIDTH used for line-breaking upstream ignores marks entirely (the actual bug).
   - **CSS ground truth for typography** (`public/styles.css`, read directly, decisive): `.section-headline, .section-kicker, .section-subheading { font-family: "Sahas Sans", ... }` (sans, weight 700 for headline/kicker, 400 for subheading/deck); `.newspaper-canvas { font-family: "Sahas Serif", ... }` (body inherits serif, weight 400); `.section-body { text-align: justify; ... }` — this rule is now DEAD for the new engine because composed lines render as `.section-composed`/`.section-body-line` absolutely-positioned spans, never inside a `.section-body` container, so the persisted `text_align`/`textAlign` field (real, already fully wired end-to-end: `typography-panel.js`'s `ALIGNMENTS=[left,center,right,justify]`, `section-model.js` default `"left"`, `pageSection.service.js`, `page.repository.js`'s `text_align = COALESCE($29,...)`) is currently silently ignored by the new compose.js.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`public/editor/compose/shaper.js`** (NEW FILE, fully written and committed to disk in this phase, NOT yet git-committed) — the HarfBuzz-backed exact shaping module. Full content as written:
     ```js
     // Real Devanagari shaping. This is the exact authority font-metrics.js
     // claimed to be and was not.
     // [... extensive header documenting the measured overstatement table ...]
     
     const FONT_FILES = {
       'serif/400': '/assets/fonts/NotoSerifDevanagari-Regular.ttf',
       'serif/700': '/assets/fonts/NotoSerifDevanagari-Bold.ttf',
       'sans/400': '/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Regular.ttf',
       'sans/700': '/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Bold.ttf',
     };
     
     function faceKey(family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const stack = String(family).toLowerCase().includes('sans') ? 'sans' : 'serif';
       return `${stack}/${Number(weight) >= 600 ? 700 : 400}`;
     }
     
     async function readFontFile(path) { /* Node: fs read via import.meta.url-derived root; browser: fetch() */ }
     
     async function loadHarfBuzz() {
       if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions?.node) return import('harfbuzzjs');
       return import('/vendor/harfbuzz/index.mjs');
     }
     
     const fonts = new Map();
     let ready = null;
     
     export function ensureShaperReady() {
       if (ready) return ready;
       ready = (async () => {
         let hb;
         try { hb = await loadHarfBuzz(); } catch { return false; }
         await Promise.all(Object.entries(FONT_FILES).map(async ([key, path]) => {
           try {
             const bytes = await readFontFile(path);
             const blob = new hb.Blob(bytes);
             const face = new hb.Face(blob);
             const font = new hb.Font(face);
             font.setScale(face.upem, face.upem);
             fonts.set(key, { hb, face, font, upem: face.upem });
           } catch { /* missing face -> caller falls back for that weight/family */ }
         }));
         return fonts.size > 0;
       })();
       return ready;
     }
     
     export function isShaperReady() { return fonts.size > 0; }
     function shapedFace(family, weight) { return fonts.get(faceKey(family, weight)) || fonts.get('serif/400') || null; }
     
     const shapeCache = new Map();
     const CACHE_LIMIT = 20000;
     
     export function shapeWidthEm(text, family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const value = String(text || '');
       if (!value) return 0;
       const face = shapedFace(family, weight);
       if (!face) return null; // explicit null, never silently 0
       const key = `${faceKey(family, weight)} ${value}`;
       const hit = shapeCache.get(key);
       if (hit !== undefined) return hit;
       const buffer = new face.hb.Buffer();
       buffer.addText(value);
       buffer.guessSegmentProperties();
       face.hb.shape(face.font, buffer);
       const positions = buffer.getGlyphPositions();
       const em = positions.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.xAdvance, 0) / face.upem;
       if (shapeCache.size > CACHE_LIMIT) shapeCache.clear();
       shapeCache.set(key, em);
       return em;
     }
     
     export function shapeWidthPx(text, fontPx, family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const em = shapeWidthEm(text, family, weight);
       return em === null ? null : em * (Number(fontPx) || 0);
     }
     
     export function shapeRun(text, { family = 'serif', weight = 400, fontPx = 16 } = {}) {
       const face = shapedFace(family, weight);
       if (!face) return null;
       const buffer = new face.hb.Buffer();
       buffer.addText(String(text || ''));
       buffer.guessSegmentProperties();
       face.hb.shape(face.font, buffer);
       const infos = buffer.getGlyphInfos();
       const positions = buffer.getGlyphPositions();
       const scale = fontPx / face.upem;
       let width = 0;
       const glyphs = infos.map((info, i) => {
         const pos = positions[i];
         const glyph = { glyphId: info.codepoint, cluster: info.cluster,
           xAdvance: pos.xAdvance*scale, xOffset: pos.xOffset*scale, yOffset: pos.yOffset*scale, x: width+pos.xOffset*scale };
         width += pos.xAdvance * scale;
         return glyph;
       });
       return { width, glyphs, ready: true };
     }
     ```
     Verified working end-to-end via a direct smoke test (`node ./shapertest.mjs` from project root): `ensureShaperReady()`→true, and produced exactly the expected shaped widths matching the earlier raw-HarfBuzz verification (क्ष=0.6950em/11.12px@16, ज्ञान=1.35em, श्री=0.885em, कर्म=1.267em, शेतकऱ्यांसाठी=4.644em, ज्ञानेश्वर=2.41em; sans/700 `विज्ञान`=2.523em; `shapeRun('क्ष',{fontPx:32})` → width 22.24, exactly 1 glyph).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **First harfbuzzjs shaping attempt produced all-zero widths**: my first smoke-test script explicitly called `buffer.setScript('Deva'); buffer.setLanguage('mr'); buffer.setDirection('ltr');` without calling `buffer.guessSegmentProperties()`. Result: `xAdvance: 0` for every glyph, and glyph-count exactly equal to codepoint-count (no real GSUB substitution happening at all) — e.g. `क् ष` (3 codepoints) → 3 glyphs, 0 width. Fixed by switching to the idiomatic `buffer.guessSegmentProperties()` call (dropping the manual script/language/direction calls entirely), which immediately produced correct results (क → xAdvance 711, matching the already-known hmtx value exactly, and क्ष → 1 glyph with real width). Root cause not fully diagnosed (likely a buffer-properties ordering/interaction requirement specific to harfbuzzjs's binding), but the fix is confirmed correct and is now the pattern used in the final `shaper.js`.

```js
  const v = String(value).toLowerCase();
  if (
    v.includes("sans") ||
    v.includes("arial") ||
    v.includes("helvetica")
  ) {
    return {
      key: "sans",
      css: "'Noto Sans Devanagari', sans-serif",
    };
  }

  return {

    css: "'Noto Serif Devanagari', serif",
  };
}
```

```js
  const writing = document.getElementById("edWritingSurface");
  writing?.classList.add("is-body-target");
  writing?.scrollIntoView({
    behavior: "smooth",
    block: "nearest"
  });

  requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    if (!quill) return;
    quill.focus();

    const selection = quill.getSelection();
    if (!selection) {
      const length = Math.max(0, quill.getLength() - 1);
      quill.setSelection(length, 0, "silent");
    }
  });
}
```

# 4. FIRST TASK — FIX THE CURRENT LINE-HEIGHT DESIGN MISTAKE

Do this **before Phase C masthead work**.

The latest commit `1ea030d` fixed inline-size overlap by finding the largest inline font anywhere in the entire body and using that height for the whole body's band grid.

That prevents overlap but damages fill.

Example:

```text
base body = 16px

one selected word = 40px
```

Current behavior can make **every line** roughly 40px-sized even though only one line contains the large word.

That can turn a previously fitting article into overset and create excessive whitespace.

This violates the main goal of accurate fill.

## Required result

Only the line that actually contains the larger run should get the larger line box.

Example:

```text
normal line → normal height
normal line → normal height
40px word line → larger height
normal line → normal height
normal line → normal height
```

Do not use one maximum font size for the entire flow.

---

# 5. Implement variable per-line body height

Primary file:

```text
public/editor/compose/compose.js
```

The algorithm must remain deterministic and bounded.

For each line:

```text
1. Start from base body line height.
2. Query legal intervals for that provisional vertical band.
3. Fit candidate text/runs into the interval.
4. Determine the maximum actual line-box requirement of runs ON THAT LINE.
5. If required height differs materially:
      query obstacles again using the larger vertical band
      and refit this line once.
6. Finalize the line.
7. Next Y = this finalized line's real bottom.
```

Maximum two passes per line.

Pseudo:

```js
function composeBodyLineAt({
  y,
  column,
  remaining,
  baseStyle,
  ...
}) {
  const baseHeight =
    baseStyle.fontPx *
    baseStyle.lineHeight;

  let bandHeight = baseHeight;
  let result = null;

  for (let pass = 0; pass < 2; pass += 1) {
    const intervals = viableIntervalsForBand(
      column,
      y,
      y + bandHeight,
      images,
      ...
    );

    result = fitBodyLine(
      intervals,
      remaining,
      ...
    );

    if (!result) break;

    const requiredHeight = Math.max(
      baseHeight,
      ...result.runs.map((run) =>
        run.fontPx *
        minLineHeightFor(
          run.family,
          run.weight
        )
      )
    );

    if (
      Math.abs(requiredHeight - bandHeight)
      < 0.25
    ) {
      break;
    }

    bandHeight = requiredHeight;
  }

  if (!result) return null;

  return {
    ...result,
    y,
    height: bandHeight,
    bottom: y + bandHeight
  };
}
```

Adapt to current interval/pour implementation instead of blindly copying names.

The critical invariant is:

```text
line height depends only on the runs actually placed on that line
```

Image obstacle sampling must use the whole final vertical line band.

# 12. Repository structural repair

File:

```text
src/repositories/page.repository.js
```

Add an idempotent helper approximately:

```js
async function ensureStructuralTemplateFrames(
  pageId,
  { tx } = {}
) {
  const db = tx || pool;

  const page =
    await findPageMeta(pageId, db);

  if (!page) return null;

  const template =
    resolveTemplateForPage(page);

  const stored =
    await listSectionKeys(pageId, db);

  const existing =
    new Set(stored);

  const created = [];

  for (const section of template.sections) {
    if (
      !isStructuralTemplateFrame(section)
    ) {
      continue;
    }

    if (existing.has(section.key)) {
      continue;
    }

    await insertTemplateSection(
      pageId,
      section,
      db
    );

    created.push(section.key);
  }

  return { created };
}
```

Reuse existing repository SQL/helpers rather than creating duplicate insertion logic.

# BUG 1 — LARGE INLINE RUN NEAR THE BOTTOM CAN STILL REPORT `FITS` WHILE PAINTING OUTSIDE THE FRAME

Current `fillRow()` approximately does:

```js
if (
  Math.abs(requiredHeight - height) < 0.25
  || pass === 1
  || !cursor.hasRoom(requiredHeight)
) {
  break;
}
```

The `!cursor.hasRoom(requiredHeight)` branch is wrong.

Current behavior:

```text
base body line fits vertically
↓
line contains a 40px selected word
↓
actual required line height is ~62px
↓
62px does NOT fit before frame bottom
↓
fillRow keeps the first base-height attempt
↓
cursor commits ~25px
↓
40px word can visually extend beyond the frame
↓
fitState can still be FITS
↓
no overset/violation
```

I reproduced this against the current uploaded source.

A configuration around:

```js
{
  width: 180,
  height: 95,
  padding: 10,
  bodyFontPx: 16,
  lineHeight: 1.25,
  columnCount: 1
}
```

with a final `data-sahas-size=40` token can currently produce approximately:

```text
fitState: FITS
line.height: ~24.88
actual 40px run requirement: ~62.2
violations: []
```

This is unacceptable.

## Correct behavior

If the candidate row needs more height than the current column has:

**do not consume the text**
**do not commit the short row**
**do not paint it with an undersized line box**

Instead:

```text
retry the SAME unconsumed text in the next column
```

If there is no later column with enough room:

```text
leave that copy in overset
```

or emit an explicit hard violation.

The composition must never say FITS while a run requires more vertical space than its line owns.

### Suggested implementation

Let `fillRow()` return a retry signal:

```js
if (
  requiredHeight > height + 0.25
  && !cursor.hasRoom(requiredHeight)
) {
  return {
    retryNextColumn: true
  };
}
```

Caller:

```js
const result = fillRow(...);

if (result?.retryNextColumn) {
  colIndex += 1;
  continue;
}
```

Important:

* `index` must remain unchanged.
* `paraCharOffset` must remain unchanged.
* current cursor must NOT commit.
* current text must be retried at the top/current position of the next column.
* if no column can accept it, normal trailing overset accounting must capture it.

Do not silently keep the undersized first pass.

### Required invariant

For every placed line:

```js
line.y + line.height <= content.bottom + tolerance
```

and:

```js
line.height >= requiredHeightOfEveryRunOnThatLine
```

Add tests.

# BUG 2 — PARAGRAPH SPACING IS CARRIED ACROSS COLUMNS USING THE OLD COLUMN'S ABSOLUTE Y

Current forced-paragraph code approximately computes:

```js
const nextY =
  lastLine.y
  + lastLine.height
  + paragraphSpacingPx;
```

and then advances the current cursor until:

```js
cursor.y >= nextY
```

That is correct only when the next paragraph continues in the **same column**.

It is wrong when the previous paragraph ends at the bottom of column 1 and the new paragraph must start in column 2.

Current behavior can become:

```text
paragraph 1 ends near y=228 in column 1
paragraphSpacingPx = 8
↓
column 1 has no room
↓
move to column 2
↓
column 2 starts at y=10
↓
code still demands y >= ~236
↓
it skips nearly the entire second column
↓
paragraph 2 becomes overset
```

I reproduced this against the current source.

Example:

```js
{
  width: 400,
  height: 260,
  padding: 10,
  bodyFontPx: 14,
  lineHeight: 1.25,
  columnCount: 2
}
```

with first paragraph approximately:

```js
'पहिला परिच्छेद मजकूर '.repeat(15)
```

and then:

```text
\n\n
दुसरा परिच्छेद नवीन स्तंभात सुरू होतो.
```

Current:

```text
paragraphSpacingPx = 0
→ paragraph 2 starts at top of column 2

paragraphSpacingPx = 8
→ paragraph 2 can disappear into overset
```

That is a real regression.

## Correct rule

Paragraph spacing is **local to a column**.

If paragraph 2 continues below paragraph 1 in the same column:

```text
apply paragraph spacing
```

If paragraph 1 exhausted the column and paragraph 2 moves to the next column:

```text
start at the normal top of the new column
```

Do NOT carry the previous column's absolute Y into the next column.

### Suggested implementation

Track which column owned the previous committed line.

For example:

```js
let lastLineColumnIndex = null;
```

When pushing a line:

```js
lastLineColumnIndex = colIndex;
```

At a forced paragraph break:

```js
if (
  paragraph.forcedBreak
  && lines.length
  && paragraphSpacingPx > 0
) {
  const previousColumn =
    lastLineColumnIndex;

  if (
    colIndex === previousColumn
  ) {
    // Apply paragraph spacing only inside this column.
    const targetY =
      lines[lines.length - 1].y
      + lines[lines.length - 1].height
      + paragraphSpacingPx;

    while (
      colIndex === previousColumn
    ) {
      if (
        !cursors[colIndex].hasRoom(bandHeight)
      ) {
        colIndex += 1;

        // NEW COLUMN:
        // spacing from old column no longer applies.
        break;
      }

      if (
        cursors[colIndex].y
        >= targetY - 0.5
      ) {
        break;
      }

      const row =
        cursors[colIndex].probe(
          bandHeight
        );

      if (!row) {
        colIndex += 1;
        break;
      }

      for (const gap of row.gaps) {
        emptyGapWidth +=
          gap.end - gap.start;
      }

      cursors[colIndex].commit(
        bandHeight
      );
    }
  }
}
```

Adapt to the cleanest current implementation.

The invariant is more important than exact code:

> **Paragraph vertical spacing must never propagate an absolute Y coordinate from one column into another.**

Add tests for:

* same-column paragraph spacing;
* paragraph ending at column bottom;
* next paragraph beginning at top of next column;
* same case where the previous paragraph's last line is a tall rich-size line.

```js
function naturalImageSize(url) {
  return new Promise(
    (resolve) => {
      const probe =
        new Image();

      probe.onload =
        () => {
          const width =
            Number(
              probe.naturalWidth
            );

          const height =
            Number(
              probe.naturalHeight
            );

          resolve(
            width > 0
            && height > 0
              ? {
                  width,
                  height,
                  ratio:
                    width /
                    height
                }
              : null
          );
        };

      probe.onerror =
        () => resolve(null);

      probe.src = url;
    }
  );
}
```

Then:

```js
const placement =
```

# 16. Normalize one image row

Suggested helper:

```js
export function imageInput(
  row
) {
  const frame = {
    x:
      Number(
        row.x_px ?? row.x
      ) || 0,

    y:
      Number(
        row.y_px ?? row.y
      ) || 0,

    width:
      Math.max(
        0,
        Number(
          row.width_px
          ?? row.width
        ) || 0
      ),

    height:
      Math.max(
        0,
        Number(
          row.height_px
          ?? row.height
        ) || 0
      )
  };

  const sourceWidth =
    Number(
      row.source_width_px
      ?? row.sourceWidth
    )
    || frame.width
    || 1;

  const sourceHeight =
    Number(
      row.source_height_px
      ?? row.sourceHeight
    )
    || frame.height
    || 1;

  return {
    frame,
    sourceWidth,
    sourceHeight,
    fitMode:
      normaliseFitMode(
        row.fit_mode
        ?? row.fitMode
      ),
    rotation:
      normaliseRotation(
        row.rotation
      ),
    flipH:
      Boolean(
        row.flip_h
        ?? row.flipH
      ),
    flipV:
      Boolean(
        row.flip_v
        ?? row.flipV
      ),
    crop: ...
  };
}
```

# 18. Fit geometry

For local unrotated target:

```text
target width = frame width
target height = frame height
```

For a quarter-turn:

```text
rotation 90/270
```

the local pre-rotation target axes are swapped.

Conceptually:

```js
const quarter =
  rotation % 180 !== 0;

const localTarget = {
  width:
    quarter
      ? frame.height
      : frame.width,

  height:
    quarter
      ? frame.width
      : frame.height
};
```

Resolve the source into this local target, then rotate the local result around the frame centre.

This preserves the current project's 90° rotation semantics without special CSS hacks in multiple places.

# 19. Contain

Given effective source crop:

```text
sw × sh
```

and local target:

```text
tw × th
```

```js
const scale =
  Math.min(
    tw / sw,
    th / sh
  );

const width =
  sw * scale;

const height =
  sh * scale;

const x =
  (tw - width) / 2;

const y =
  (th - height) / 2;
```

# 5. SCREEN → LOGICAL RECT

Current resize arithmetic operates on the visible Editor frame.

That is fine as long as the local `state.images` preview is written back in **logical block pixels**.

After `resizeRect()` returns the screen-space preview rectangle:

```js
function logicalRectFromScreen(
  rect,
  scale
) {
  return {
    x:
      Math.round(
        rect.x * scale
      ),

    y:
      Math.round(
        rect.y * scale
      ),

    width:
      Math.round(
        rect.width * scale
      ),

    height:
      Math.round(
        rect.height * scale
      )
  };
}
```

# 2. `sourcePointToFrame()`

Required transform order must match paint:

```text
source pixels
→ crop-relative coordinates
→ fitted content rectangle
→ flip H/V
→ quarter-turn rotation
→ frame coordinates
```

Use the geometry already returned by:

```js
resolvePlacedImage()
```

including:

```text
frame
crop
localTarget
localContentRect
fitMode
rotation
flipH
flipV
```

Conceptually:

```js
export function sourcePointToFrame(
  resolved,
  sourceX,
  sourceY
) {
  const {
    frame,
    crop,
    localTarget,
    localContentRect,
    flipH,
    flipV,
    rotation
  } = resolved;

  let u =
    (
      sourceX -
      crop.x
    ) /
    crop.width;

  let v =
    (
      sourceY -
      crop.y
    ) /
    crop.height;

  if (flipH) {
    u = 1 - u;
  }

  if (flipV) {
    v = 1 - v;
  }

  let x =
    localContentRect.x +
    u *
    localContentRect.width;

  let y =
    localContentRect.y +
    v *
    localContentRect.height;

  const cx =
    localTarget.width / 2;

  const cy =
    localTarget.height / 2;

  const dx = x - cx;
  const dy = y - cy;

  switch (
    ((rotation % 360) + 360) % 360
  ) {
    case 0:
      break;

    case 90:
      [x, y] = [
        cx - dy,
        cy + dx
      ];
      break;

    case 180:
      [x, y] = [
        cx - dx,
        cy - dy
      ];
      break;

    case 270:
      [x, y] = [
        cx + dy,
        cy - dx
      ];
      break;

    default:
      // Do not silently claim exactness.
      return null;
  }

  return {
    x:
      frame.x +
      frame.width / 2 -
      localTarget.width / 2 +
      x,

    y:
      frame.y +
      frame.height / 2 -
      localTarget.height / 2 +
      y
  };
}
```

This pseudocode is a guide.

**Verify signs/centres against the browser paint.**

Do not blindly copy it if current `localTarget` quarter-turn semantics require a different centre conversion.

# 7. FIX `placementsByEdition()`

Join `media_assets`.

Return every composition-affecting field:

```sql
SELECT
  si.page_section_id,

  si.x_px,
  si.y_px,
  si.width_px,
  si.height_px,

  si.crop_x_px,
  si.crop_y_px,
  si.crop_width_px,
  si.crop_height_px,

  si.rotation,
  si.flip_h,
  si.flip_v,

  si.shape,
  si.stand_off_px,
  si.mask,
  si.fit_mode,

  ma.width_px
    AS source_width_px,

  ma.height_px
    AS source_height_px

FROM section_images si

JOIN media_assets ma
  ON ma.id =
     si.media_asset_id

JOIN page_sections s
  ON s.id =
     si.page_section_id

JOIN pages p
  ON p.id =
     s.page_id

WHERE p.newspaper_id = $1
```

Preserve ordering.

Do this before Smart Cards.

The quarter-turn cutout transform itself is now implemented correctly through:

```text
image-geometry.js
→ sourceRectToFrameBounds()
→ exclusion.js
```

However `obstacleIntervals()` still performs an **incorrect early vertical rejection** before reaching that exact cutout path.

Current logic begins approximately:

```js
const pad = standOffPx(
  image,
  bodyFontPx
);

const box =
  boxOf(
    image,
    pad
  );

if (
  bottom <= box.top ||
  top >= box.bottom
) {
  return [];
}
```

`boxOf()` rotates the stored placement rectangle.

That does NOT match how quarter-turn painting now works.

The stored placement frame itself remains fixed.

For a 90°/270° image, `picture-style.js` first swaps the inner image's local target axes and then rotates that inner image around the fixed frame centre.

Therefore a 100×200 placement rotated 90° still visually occupies the **100×200 placement frame**.

But `boxOf()` currently treats the 100×200 frame as though the frame itself rotated and produces roughly a 200×100 vertical gate.

That can reject valid cutout occupancy before the exact transformed mask is even evaluated.

     ```js
     export function styledRuns(runText, at, marks, baseFontPx) {
       const plain = () => [{ text: runText, bold: false, italic: false, underline: false, fontPx: baseFontPx }];
       if (!marks.length || !runText) return plain();
       const end = at + runText.length;
       const relevant = marks.filter((mark) => mark.start < end && mark.end > at);
       if (!relevant.length) return plain();
       const cuts = new Set([0, runText.length]);
       for (const mark of relevant) {
         if (mark.start > at) cuts.add(mark.start - at);
         if (mark.end < end) cuts.add(mark.end - at);
       }
       const points = [...cuts].sort((a, b) => a - b);
       const runs = [];
       for (let index = 0; index < points.length - 1; index += 1) {
         const from = points[index]; const to = points[index + 1];
         if (to <= from) continue;
         const active = relevant.filter((mark) => mark.start <= at + from && mark.end >= at + to);
         const sizeMark = active.find((mark) => mark.tag === 'size');
         runs.push({
           text: runText.slice(from, to),
           bold: active.some((mark) => mark.tag === 'b'),
           italic: active.some((mark) => mark.tag === 'i'),
           underline: active.some((mark) => mark.tag === 'u'),
           fontPx: sizeMark ? sizeMark.value : baseFontPx,
         });
       }
       return runs.length ? runs : plain();
     }
     ```

Top-level function `hb.shape(font, buffer)`.
   - **Dual Node/browser module loading pattern** (already established by font-metrics.js, now replicated in shaper.js): Node reaches the real package via `import('harfbuzzjs')`/`node:fs/promises` reading from `public/assets/fonts/`; browser fetches from a vendored, statically-served copy — new addition: `public/vendor/harfbuzz/` (containing `index.mjs`, `harfbuzz.js`, `harfbuzz.wasm`, `index.d.mts`, `LICENSE`), imported via `import('/vendor/harfbuzz/index.mjs')`. Confirmed via `server.js:45` (`app.use(express.static(path.join(__dirname,"public")))`) that this will be correctly served. Confirmed via inspecting `harfbuzz.js`'s emscripten glue that `.wasm` location is derived relative to `import.meta.url`, so directory-relative vendoring works in both runtimes without extra configuration.
   - **UAX #29 grapheme clusters** (`Intl.Segmenter('mr',{granularity:'grapheme'})`, existing, correct, unchanged) — text is only ever measured/cut at akshara boundaries via `graphemes.js`'s `clusters()`/`breakPieces()`/`trimEndClusters()`/`clusterCount()`.
   - **Forced vs optional line breaks**: `graphemes.js`'s `BREAK_AFTER = /[\s।॥\-–—/]/` currently treats `\n` (which matches `\s`) as an ORDINARY optional break — confirmed bug, needs a paragraph-aware preprocessing layer (planned to live in `compose.js`, not `graphemes.js`) that distinguishes single `\n` (line/list forced break) from `\n\n` (paragraph forced break, normally also gets extra visual spacing — deferred in this pass per an explicit, documented scope decision).
   - **Rich text infrastructure** (`public/editor/layout/rich-text.js`, existing, correct, being built ON rather than replaced): `plainText()`, `textWithMarks()` (returns `{text, marks:[{start,end,tag}]}`, tag ∈ {b,i,u}), `markRun()`, `sanitise()`, `fromPlainText()`. Critically: `plainText()` and `textWithMarks()` produce IDENTICAL underlying `text` for the same HTML input (same tag/newline/entity normalization pipeline), which is WHY `render.js`'s currently-separate re-derivation of marks via character offsets happens to already be positionally correct today, even though the WIDTH used for line-breaking upstream ignores marks entirely (the actual bug).

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`public/editor/compose/shaper.js`** (NEW FILE, fully written and committed to disk in this phase, NOT yet git-committed) — the HarfBuzz-backed exact shaping module. Full content as written:
     ```js
     // Real Devanagari shaping. This is the exact authority font-metrics.js
     // claimed to be and was not.
     // [... extensive header documenting the measured overstatement table ...]
     
     const FONT_FILES = {
       'serif/400': '/assets/fonts/NotoSerifDevanagari-Regular.ttf',
       'serif/700': '/assets/fonts/NotoSerifDevanagari-Bold.ttf',
       'sans/400': '/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Regular.ttf',
       'sans/700': '/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Bold.ttf',
     };
     
     function faceKey(family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const stack = String(family).toLowerCase().includes('sans') ? 'sans' : 'serif';
       return `${stack}/${Number(weight) >= 600 ? 700 : 400}`;
     }
     
     async function readFontFile(path) { /* Node: fs read via import.meta.url-derived root; browser: fetch() */ }
     
     async function loadHarfBuzz() {
       if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions?.node) return import('harfbuzzjs');
       return import('/vendor/harfbuzz/index.mjs');
     }
     
     const fonts = new Map();
     let ready = null;
     
     export function ensureShaperReady() {
       if (ready) return ready;
       ready = (async () => {
         let hb;
         try { hb = await loadHarfBuzz(); } catch { return false; }
         await Promise.all(Object.entries(FONT_FILES).map(async ([key, path]) => {
           try {
             const bytes = await readFontFile(path);
             const blob = new hb.Blob(bytes);
             const face = new hb.Face(blob);
             const font = new hb.Font(face);
             font.setScale(face.upem, face.upem);
             fonts.set(key, { hb, face, font, upem: face.upem });
           } catch { /* missing face -> caller falls back for that weight/family */ }
         }));
         return fonts.size > 0;
       })();
       return ready;
     }
     
     export function isShaperReady() { return fonts.size > 0; }
     function shapedFace(family, weight) { return fonts.get(faceKey(family, weight)) || fonts.get('serif/400') || null; }
     
     const shapeCache = new Map();
     const CACHE_LIMIT = 20000;
     
     export function shapeWidthEm(text, family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const value = String(text || '');
       if (!value) return 0;
       const face = shapedFace(family, weight);
       if (!face) return null; // explicit null, never silently 0
       const key = `${faceKey(family, weight)} ${value}`;
       const hit = shapeCache.get(key);
       if (hit !== undefined) return hit;
       const buffer = new face.hb.Buffer();
       buffer.addText(value);
       buffer.guessSegmentProperties();
       face.hb.shape(face.font, buffer);
       const positions = buffer.getGlyphPositions();
       const em = positions.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.xAdvance, 0) / face.upem;
       if (shapeCache.size > CACHE_LIMIT) shapeCache.clear();
       shapeCache.set(key, em);
       return em;
     }
     
     export function shapeWidthPx(text, fontPx, family = 'serif', weight = 400) {
       const em = shapeWidthEm(text, family, weight);
       return em === null ? null : em * (Number(fontPx) || 0);
     }
     
     export function shapeRun(text, { family = 'serif', weight = 400, fontPx = 16 } = {}) {
       const face = shapedFace(family, weight);
       if (!face) return null;
       const buffer = new face.hb.Buffer();
       buffer.addText(String(text || ''));
       buffer.guessSegmentProperties();
       face.hb.shape(face.font, buffer);
       const infos = buffer.getGlyphInfos();
       const positions = buffer.getGlyphPositions();
       const scale = fontPx / face.upem;
       let width = 0;
       const glyphs = infos.map((info, i) => {
         const pos = positions[i];
         const glyph = { glyphId: info.codepoint, cluster: info.cluster,
           xAdvance: pos.xAdvance*scale, xOffset: pos.xOffset*scale, yOffset: pos.yOffset*scale, x: width+pos.xOffset*scale };
         width += pos.xAdvance * scale;
         return glyph;
       });
       return { width, glyphs, ready: true };
     }
     ```
     Verified working end-to-end via a direct smoke test (`node ./shapertest.mjs` from project root): `ensureShaperReady()`→true, and produced exactly the expected shaped widths matching the earlier raw-HarfBuzz verification (क्ष=0.6950em/11.12px@16, ज्ञान=1.35em, श्री=0.885em, कर्म=1.267em, शेतकऱ्यांसाठी=4.644em, ज्ञानेश्वर=2.41em; sans/700 `विज्ञान`=2.523em; `shapeRun('क्ष',{fontPx:32})` → width 22.24, exactly 1 glyph).
